title: Fixtures
text:
These files are declarative inputs. They are never loaded automatically.

bootstrap-registry.json supplies local actors, versioned methods, the pinned tool/configuration/environment baseline, internal cid/ifc schemes, positive evidence-profile definitions with explicit scope policy, the independence rule, a version-keyed intended use, and an initial version-keyed query set. Profile and query seals remain explicit later workflow acts.
pilot-negative-cases.json is the future pilot matrix from methodology Section 14 plus release/package-chain, identity-tuple, profile-seal, current-use/query, unified-cid, and bootstrap/advance adversarial cases. It is a test design, not synthetic evidence and not proof that acceptance criteria passed.

Loading the bootstrap is an explicit operator action:
bin/ci-digital-concept-index record import \
  --input fixtures/bootstrap-registry.json
No fixture was loaded while authoring this application.

title: Design Decisions
text: Use SQLite as the canonical append-only store; JSON/TSV are derived exchange views. This gives local transactions, foreign keys, constraints, and audit queries without a service dependency.

title: Design Decisions
text: Use SQLite as the canonical append-only store; JSON/TSV are derived exchange views. This gives local transactions, foreign keys, constraints, and audit queries without a service dependency.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-002 — Standard Library Only
Use CPython standard library and sqlite3; pin no third-party packages. This minimizes supply-chain and network dependence. Analytical scale/Parquet remains future work.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-003 — No Internal Document Parsers
Support UTF-8 plain/Markdown identity import and provenance-complete external extraction import. Do not invoke PDF/OCR/office/HTML parsers or subprocesses. Fidelity remains an explicit external derivation concern.

title: Design Decisions
section: ADR-004 — Record Families Never Promote In Place
text:
ADR-004 — Record Families Never Promote In Place
Expose named new-record commands rather than promote, update, or delete. Observation, candidate, claim, review, decision, release, and publication IDs remain distinct.

title: Design Decisions
section: ADR-005 — Version Records Own Stable IDs
text:
ADR-005 — Version Records Own Stable IDs
Each immutable version row receives a stable nonreusable ID. Logical continuity uses keys, versions, supersession, validity intervals, and events. Tombstones preserve historical resolution.

title: Design Decisions
section: ADR-006 — Typed Warrants Prevent Circular Domain Evidence
text:
ADR-006 — Typed Warrants Prevent Circular Domain Evidence
Require E-DOMAIN to resolve an authenticated normative/authoritative external domain warrant and E-PROJECT to resolve an approved versioned project requirement. Informative warrants and annotation/review/approval cannot satisfy support gates.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-007 — Profile Groups Express Alternatives
Different requirement groups are cumulative; alternatives inside a group express domain or project warrant. Seal the canonical profile plus a non-empty set of positive requirements, bind every claim to the exact profile version/type/seal, and enforce count/ISF before acceptance.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-008 — Evidence Membership Is Normalized
Store exact aggregate/edge/similarity membership in relational tables, require every evidence/source/segment value to identify one chain, and derive the hash from it. A hash or count alone is not traceability. Projections copy membership and add no independent support.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-009 — All Nodes Precede Edges
graph_nodes is independent from edge construction. The observation view unions nodes first, preserving isolates and preventing an edge-list artifact from defining the inventory.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-010 — Domain Schemes Remain Independent
Version internal cid and ifc schemes separately from external ext schemes. Cross-scheme correspondence is always a scoped mapping with loss/conditions, never label-based merging.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-011 — Approval Is Not Publication
Freeze a non-recursive release-content artifact first, create independent current V&V/retrieval/assurance records, then freeze a separate complete approval-package artifact without mutating release content. Package versions extend one explicit immutable current-head chain per release; a superseded package cannot receive a new approval or publication. Approve and publish the package hash. First success is explicit bootstrap; later success advances from the immediate current release. Only successful or rollback events affect current state; failures are audit history.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-012 — Unknown Is Not Zero
Null sessions produce unavailable SF; unresolved lineage is excluded/reported; partial authentication remains partial; inconclusive checks remain inconclusive. The app never completes missing evidence by assumption.

title: Design Decisions
text:
ADR-013 — Ontology Features Are Deferred
No RDF/SKOS/OWL/SHACL export or reasoner is included. Introduce them only after approved competency questions, formal identity/equivalence/inference semantics, constraints, and logical tests justify ontology status.

title: Design Decisions
section: ADR-014 — Definition Claims Bind Exact Text
text:
ADR-014 — Definition Claims Bind Exact Text
Concept publication requires a normalized concept_definition_claims row that binds the claim to the exact concept ID, version, definition, scope note, and applicability. Scheme-membership claims cannot substitute for a reviewed definition.

title: Design Decisions
section: ADR-015 — Current V&V Is the Terminal Supersession Head
text:
ADR-015 — Current V&V Is the Terminal Supersession Head
Verification, intended-use, query-set, validation, and retrieval records form immutable supersession chains. Validation/retrieval are current only with the terminal approved use, matching user group/context, and current sealed query/relevance baseline, so evolution or a later fail/not-fit immediately invalidates older fitness evidence.

title: Design Decisions
section: ADR-016 — Release Items Resolve One Actual Version Policy
text:
ADR-016 — Release Items Resolve One Actual Version Policy
Each allowed item family has one code/SQL version rule, canonical row snapshot, and hash. The non-recursive release-content hash must equal its artifact identity/output; each version in the separate linear approval-package chain hashes the complete required frozen baseline closure. Both identities and the current package head are recomputed at approval, publication, and export.

Native-Domain Separation

title: Standards Baseline
Security
text: The local operator may ingest untrusted text, code, tool output, JSON metadata, or externally extracted document text. Primary risks are command/code execution, SQL injection, path escape, data leakage, provenance spoofing, semantic privilege escalation, identifier reuse, and release tampering.

title: Security
text: The local operator may ingest untrusted text, code, tool output, JSON metadata, or externally extracted document text. Primary risks are command/code execution, SQL injection, path escape, data leakage, provenance spoofing, semantic privilege escalation, identifier reuse, and release tampering.

title: Security
text:
Controls

No Active Content

The app has no network client, shell invocation, plugin loader, template evaluator, dynamic Python import, or model endpoint.
Source files are opened only as UTF-8 text.
PDF/OCR/parser execution is unsupported; externally produced text is inert imported data with provenance.
Ingested strings are never executed as SQL. Values use SQLite parameters.



Path Containment

Source paths must resolve under configured source_roots.
Database and export roots must resolve inside the app directory.
Export-relative paths cannot escape exports/.
Symlink resolution occurs before containment checks.



SQL Boundary

Dynamic table/view names are checked against SQLite inventory or fixed allowlists.
Identifiers pass a conservative ASCII identifier pattern before interpolation.
Record values are parameterized.
Foreign keys and recursive triggers are enabled on every connection.



Integrity and Nonrepudiation Limits

SHA-256 detects accidental/tampering changes but is not a digital signature.
Actor IDs and authority strings are registry assertions; this version has no authentication service.
External locators are not fetched or authenticated automatically.
authentication_status and completeness_status must therefore remain evidence-specific and may be partial/unavailable.



Semantic Privilege Separation

E-DOMAIN/E-PROJECT cannot be created by relabeling informative warrants or annotation/review/decision rows; typed authority/warrant FKs and triggers enforce their qualifying sources.
Claim type/version is bound to the exact recomputed seal of a non-vacuous positive profile, and one cid activation rule covers explicit scope, predicate namespace, and endpoints.
Reviewer differs from claim asserter; approval inputs differ from review/V&V executor; publisher differs from approver.
Observation predicates are prohibited in semantic assertions.
Projection membership cannot increase independent evidence.



Release Integrity

Release item canonical records/hashes and the non-recursive content artifact hash are recomputed independently of stored values.
Post-V&V approval packages freeze the exact required baseline closure in immutable snapshots; package hash, artifact identity/output, release-content link, and linear supersession head all recompute.
Approval targets an exact release/version/current package head and links explicit current V&V/retrieval/assurance inputs.
Successful publication checks the exact approved package hash, current gates, exclusive bootstrap/advance state, rollback preparation, and role separation.
Export requires the release to be current, validates its publication-bound package, emits both identities/frozen snapshots, and refuses overwrite of a non-empty destination.

title: Security
text:
Local Hardening

Keep source/migration/config files read-only for routine operators.
Restrict var/ and exports/ to the owning account.
Do not store secrets in source records, logs, JSON specs, SQLite, or exports.
Review rights/access notes before packaging evidence.
Treat copied databases/exports as sensitive research artifacts.
Verify executable/runtime paths independently; PYTHON launcher override is an operator-controlled trust boundary.

title: Security
text:
Known Limits
No OS sandbox, encrypted database, signatures, authenticated identities, access-control service, secret manager, malware scanner, parser sandbox, or remote audit service is included. A future network/UI deployment requires a new threat model, change request, verification, and intended-use validation.

title: Lifecycle
text:
Claim State
(none) -> proposed
proposed -> reviewed_accepted | reviewed_rejected | superseded
reviewed_accepted -> stale | superseded
stale -> reviewed_accepted | reviewed_rejected | superseded
Rejected and superseded versions are terminal. A changed proposition normally receives a new claim version; a stale unchanged proposition can receive a new review event after its impact obligations are completed. current_claim_state selects the latest timestamp/event ID deterministically.

title: Lifecycle
text:
Change Request State
(none) -> open
open -> accepted | rejected | closed
accepted -> implemented | closed
implemented -> closed
The request row remains immutable; current_change_request_state derives state from events.

title: Lifecycle
Lifecycle
text:
Publication Outcomes

successful bootstrap: permitted only when the channel has no earlier effective event; exact approved package hash, explicit bootstrap evidence, current package gates, publication procedure, event evidence, and publisher/approver separation are mandatory, while every rollback field is null.
successful advance: permitted only after bootstrap/effective history; it binds the exact approved package hash and names the immediate effective current release as its distinct rollback release, which must have succeeded earlier on that channel; rollback procedure/evidence and all normal gates are mandatory.
failed: exact approved package binding and event evidence are mandatory; bootstrap/rollback state fields are null and current release is unchanged.
rolled_back: the event’s release must equal the immediate effective current release; its distinct target must have succeeded earlier on the same channel using the package that remains that target release’s valid current package head; exact outgoing-package binding plus rollback procedure/evidence are mandatory.

current_published_releases selects the latest effective (succeeded or rolled_back) event per channel by (event_time, publication_event_id). For rollback state, it resolves both the restored release and that release’s latest earlier successful approval package rather than treating the rollback event’s package as the restored package. Current package eligibility is evaluated against this effective channel head; immutable historical publication rows retain their original structural validity instead of being retroactively reclassified when a package is superseded. A new effective event must be strictly later under that ordering. Failed events are audit evidence only and carry no rollback fields.

title: Lifecycle
text:
Impact and Staleness
workflow impact begins with changed items, expands known claim/evidence/release/intended-use dependencies, merges declared dependencies, hashes the closure, and stores each impact item. Open/blocked assessment creates stale events for previously accepted dependent claims. The assessment selects reverify, revalidate, both, or neither_with_rationale; one cannot substitute for the other.

title: Lifecycle
text:
Deprecation and Retirement
Deprecation preserves identity, history, retrieval treatment, validity, replacement, rationale, and migration plan. Retirement is blocked until impact is complete, exact retirement approval exists, and live semantic/mapping/published-release dependencies are removed or dispositioned. A successful retirement creates a tombstone; the target stable ID remains resolvable forever and cannot be reused.

title: Domain Policy
Domain Policy
text:
Qualifying Support

E-DOMAIN is valid only when it names a typed domain_warrant bound to a versioned external scheme, the same authenticated source version, exact locator, normative or authoritative status, and applicable scope. An informative warrant is retained as provenance but excluded from admissible support, counts, ISF, and reviewed graph/release gates.
E-PROJECT is valid only when it names an approved versioned requirements row.
Annotation, review, approval, publication, source frequency, and graph topology cannot be relabeled as either class.
A claim profile binds support role and evidence class; domain/project alternatives share one requirement group.

title: Domain Policy
Domain Policy
text:
Binding Negative Rules

Generic software “verification” and IC/UVM verification remain distinct definitions.
Telecommunications material remains outside cid without exact IC applicability; words such as network or channel do not bridge the boundary.
Brazil/geography/policy is metadata, ext, or excluded—not a VLSI concept because of sponsorship or co-location.
Construction/BIM “digital twin” remains outside cid absent separately evidenced IC use.
Database, OAuth, build, graph, NLP, and formal-logic implementation concepts belong to ifc unless an exact independent VLSI meaning is admitted.
Visual clustering, adjacency, and projection remain presentation/observation evidence.

The non-negotiable pilot gate is zero known provenance-class or domain-boundary violations.

title: Architecture
text: The system owns a local append-only evidence and governance ledger. SQLite owns relational integrity and immutable transition guards; Python owns deterministic transformations, canonical serialization, path policy, and explicit command orchestration. Neither storage nor a graph view owns semantic truth.

title: Architecture
text:
Controlled Flow
source reference/bytes
  -> acquisition activity + source artifact/version + reviewed routing history
  -> extraction derivation + exact source/input/output/text/spans/quality
  -> segment derivation + provenance/language/scope
  -> normalization -> tokenization -> n-grams -> measures
  -> all-node observation graph
  -> explicit candidate nomination
  -> sealed non-vacuous profile -> term/concept + atomic scoped claim package
  -> independent semantic review
  -> immutable release-content candidate
  -> current verification + approved-use/query/relevance validation + retrieval + assurance
  -> immutable versioned approval-package head with complete frozen release-relative closure
  -> independent approval of that package
  -> bootstrap, advance, failed, or rollback publication event
  -> current-release derived view
  -> change/impact/reverification/revalidation/deprecation/retirement
Each arrow creates a new record and typed link. No command mutates an earlier observation into a candidate, candidate into a claim, claim into a decision, or decision into publication.

title: Architecture
text:
Four Mandatory Views

provenance_evidence_view
Unifies agents, source identities/routing/revisions, acquisition activities and tools, configuration applicability, derivation runs and normalized input/tool/output links, artifact identity state, extraction records/spans, segments/quoted-source links, evidence items, lineage groups, and lineage links. It is an audit view, not a semantic graph.


observation_graph
Unifies graph-node rows, token/n-gram occurrences, aggregate measures, co-occurrence, precedence, independent source-distribution similarity-signal records, and projected analytical edges. Nodes are selected independently of edges, preserving isolates. obs: predicates never enter semantic assertions.


reviewed_semantic_graph
Includes concept definitions, semantic assertions, and scoped mappings only when their exact claim is currently reviewed_accepted, its profile/ISF passes, and its domain firewall passes. A concept is not admitted merely because any unrelated accepted claim references it.


release_governance_view
Unifies intended uses, requirements, query sets/evaluations, reviews, verification, validation, assurance arguments, approvals, releases, publication attempts, changes, impacts, deprecations, and retirements.

title: Architecture
text:
Trust Boundaries

Source boundary: configured read roots; content remains inert data.
Write boundary: SQLite under var/ and deterministic files under exports/.
Semantic boundary: cid, ext, and ifc schemes remain independent; explicit scope, a cid predicate, or either cid endpoint activates the same claim firewall.
Governance boundary: executor, reviewer, approver, and publisher acts use distinct records and are checked for actor separation.
Publication boundary: the immutable release-content hash is never extended after V&V; publication binds the separate approved package hash, and only a valid bootstrap/advance or rollback event changes the derived current-release view.

title: Architecture
text:
Recovery
SQLite transactions own atomic local writes. A failed command rolls back its entire transaction. Existing immutable rows and previous successful publications remain intact. Recovery is rerunning a corrected command with a new record/run/event ID; it is never editing or deleting the failed historical record.

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
A deterministic, local-first Python and SQLite implementation of the evidence-first methodology in the concept graph methodology.
The application preserves separate immutable record families for source evidence, analytical observations, candidates, reviewed semantic claims, verification, validation, approval, releases, publication events, and lifecycle actions. It does not infer semantic truth from counts, does not use an LLM, does not call the network, and does not claim ontology status.

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
Runtime

CPython 3.11 or later.
SQLite 3.35 or later through Python’s standard-library sqlite3 module.
No third-party package, service, model, daemon, or network connection.
Writable state only under var/ and exports/ by default.

The authoritative runtime declaration is runtime.lock.json. The launcher is bin/ci-digital-concept-index.

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
Layout
bin/                  local launcher
config/               application, normalization, and environment examples
docs/                 requirements, architecture, policy, assurance, and operations
exports/              deterministic downstream files; ignored except .gitkeep
fixtures/             explicit bootstrap input and future negative-test design
migrations/           checksum-pinned SQLite schema, views, and guards
schemas/               JSON command-envelope contracts
src/                   standard-library Python package
var/                   local SQLite state; ignored except .gitkeep

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
Operator Sequence
All commands are explicit; none run automatically.
cd /home/fern/workspace/Inatel/CI-DIGITAL/worktree/software/ci-digital-concept-index

bin/ci-digital-concept-index status
bin/ci-digital-concept-index init
bin/ci-digital-concept-index record import \
  --input fixtures/bootstrap-registry.json
bin/ci-digital-concept-index validate all
The bootstrap is optional and is never evidence about a source corpus. Source acquisition records must be appended separately before extraction.

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
Explicit Workflow

Append actors, versioned procedures/tools/configurations/environments, explicit configuration-to-procedure/tool applicability, acquisition activities, source identities, versioned source-routing decisions, source artifacts, and source versions.
Run pipeline extract, segment, normalize, tokenize, ngrams, aggregate, observe, and isf with explicit JSON specs.
Run workflow nominate-term or nominate-relation; an observation never changes type.
Seal each positive non-vacuous claim profile and complete query/relevance set, then run workflow register-term, register-concept, and claim; candidates and claims keep distinct IDs.
Run workflow review, create the immutable release-content candidate, then run verify, validate-use, evaluate-retrieval, and assure as separate release-relative acts.
Run workflow finalize-release to freeze the complete post-V&V approval package, then an independent approve, then publish. A later package version must explicitly supersede the current package head for the same immutable release. The first channel success is bootstrap; later success is advance. Neither approval nor publication mutates release content.
Use change, impact, deprecate, and retire to create new lifecycle records; canonical rows are never updated or deleted.

There is intentionally no promote, update, or delete command.

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
Mandatory Views

provenance_evidence_view
observation_graph
reviewed_semantic_graph
release_governance_view

observation_graph includes registered nodes before edges, so isolates survive, and exposes source-distribution scores as independent similarity_signal records. reviewed_semantic_graph includes concept definitions only through exact reviewed claim-to-definition bindings and includes only reviewed-accepted claims whose exact evidence profile and domain firewall pass. A projected edge remains an observation and copies its root evidence membership without adding independent support.

title: CI-DIGITAL Concept Index
text:
Safety Boundaries

Plain UTF-8 and Markdown extraction are identity imports. PDF, OCR, office, HTML, and external parser results must be produced elsewhere and imported with external_import, tool/version records, span maps, quality, and uncertainty.
Input and export paths are constrained to configured roots.
Ingested text is data only. The app never executes it, imports it as Python, evaluates it as SQL, or invokes a subprocess.
Every operational timestamp is supplied in a command spec. The app never invents acquisition, derivation, review, approval, or publication time.
Claim cid governance activates from explicit cid scope, a cid predicate, or either cid endpoint and requires exact active scope plus entity-level VLSI applicability/admission. ext: and ifc: remain separate schemes; scope none is only for sealed non-semantic profiles.
Release content and post-V&V approval packages have separate canonical artifact hashes. Packages form one immutable linear version chain per release; only its current head can be newly approved or published. Publication binds the approved package hash; exports include both identities and the frozen baseline snapshots.

The entry point passes an unrecognized first argument directly to the requested tool. Useful persistent protocol processes from the same image include:

title: CI-DIGITAL language toolbox
text:
Next boundary
If a common broker or protocol adapter is authorized later, Go is the selected implementation language. That choice is recorded here without implying that the broker already exists. The present image contains only independently callable tools and the small shell entry point needed to select one foreground command.

title: CI-DIGITAL language toolbox
text:
Deliberate exclusions

VS Code and its extensions remain clients, not container contents.
The extension-private Prolog server and WebAssembly Z3 runner are not stable editor-independent boundaries.
The extended SWI-Prolog packages are omitted because their dependency closure brings Python, TeX Live, documentation, and unrelated libraries into this base image.
The repository-local markdown-guard is not copied into this independently sourced toolbox.
Tcl Whitesmiths formatting is not claimed. The current Tcl formatter exposes K&R braces only; a safe Whitesmiths implementation remains a separate formatter feature requiring Tcl-aware continuation semantics and tests.
No API broker, socket service, Compose file, or remote endpoint is implemented here. Those remain a later layer if multiple clients demonstrate a concrete need for one stable front door.

title: rx_uart
text:
State Behavior

idle

rx_done = 0
rx_error = 0
if rx_start && !rx, transition to start_bit



start_bit

if count == 7 && rx, transition to idle
else if count == 15, transition to recv_data
else remain in start_bit



recv_data

if count == 7, sample rx into datard using {rx, datard[7:1]}
if count == 15 && bit_count == (length - 1), drive rx_out, compute parity, and transition to check_parity or check_first_stop



check_parity

if count == 7, compare rx with parity and update rx_error
if count == 15, transition to check_first_stop



check_first_stop

if count == 7, compare rx with 1'b1 and update rx_error
if count == 15, transition to check_sec_stop when stop2 is set, otherwise transition to done



check_sec_stop

if count == 7, compare rx with 1'b1 and update rx_error
if count == 15, transition to done



done

rx_done = 1
rx_error = 0
transition to idle

title: rx_uart
text:
Counter Behavior

count tracks sub-bit timing and advances from 0 to 15
bit_count advances once per received data bit in recv_data
both counters clear in idle and done

title: rx_uart
text:
Data-Length Handling
When the final data bit is reached, rx_out is selected from datard by length:

5: datard[7:3]
6: datard[7:2]
7: datard[7:1]
8: datard[7:0]

title: rx_uart
text:
Observed Behavior

In the observed receive scenario with an 8-bit frame carrying 8'hA5, parity disabled, and one stop bit, rx_out became 8'hA5 and rx_done asserted at frame completion.
In the same scenario, rx_error remained 0.

On tx_done_rise:

ready_to_transmit_tx <= '1

Else if tx_start:

ready_to_transmit_tx <= '0

If ~txd:

tx_start <= '0

Current interpretation:

the byte data path still completes
the status/error path does not currently reflect the expected parity-error event

title: Repository Boundary
text:
Scope
The concept concerns how repository roles, audiences, control surfaces, sources, working artifacts, and implementations are distinguished before paths are derived or changed.
It does not establish the agent’s early four-way taxonomy as final, treat current directories as proof of semantic membership, or authorize moves merely because a structure is proposed.

title: Repository Boundary
text:
Development through interaction

1. File-tree structure exposed boundary mistakes
The engineer said earlier local Codex work had made many boundary mistakes and that the file tree itself carries information about domain boundaries. The engineer required the repository to be normalized while retaining the existing work (Segments 0034–0039).
This correction rejected cleanup by removal but did not yet define the final architecture.


2. A four-way boundary was proposed, not adopted
The agent proposed public, work, evidence, and private as a lean boundary model. The engineer questioned the private area’s relation to agent material, and the agent reframed it as explicit project-local working material rather than hidden agent-only residue (Segments 0071–0079).
The four-way model remains an agent proposal. The engineer did not adopt it as the final tree.


3. Control and terminology were disentangled
When the engineer asked about the agent taking control of .authoring/, the agent discussed ownership and authorization. The engineer corrected that authority was not the problem; terminology around authorship, authoring, authorization, attribution, scope, and delegation had drifted and could not enter public submission in that state (Segments 0080–0091).
The agent’s terminology separation was accepted as a repository-local working frame, not as public content.


4. A root design remained only a proposal
The agent proposed keeping README, Manifest, and AGENTS at root with several top-level directories and explicitly said no files had moved (Segments 0119–0122). The engineer later returned to the missing minimal terminology and boundary model rather than adopting that design (Segments 0149–0151).


5. Roles-first derivation was proposed and then simplified
The agent proposed deriving names and paths from roles such as public orientation, authored text, operations, work, and evidence (Segments 0149–0151). Later, the engineer rejected formal domain contracts and requested small guesses, one layer at a time (Segments 0578–0584).
Roles-first derivation remains an agent hypothesis constrained by the engineer’s incremental method.

title: Worktree
text:
Scope
Worktree concerns the umbrella under which multiple self-contained, repository-shaped work directories or work units are organized inside CI-DIGITAL.
The engineer’s intended use comes from an EDA-style workspace intuition and is explicitly distinguished from Git worktrees. The term workspace was explored but is also overloaded. No vendor-derived name is treated as final authority.

title: Worktree
text:
Development through interaction

1. The engineer defined an umbrella for work directories
The engineer described worktree as an umbrella for many work directories, each resembling a single repository-shaped structure. The umbrella provides a natural place for those units (Segments 0442–0444).


2. Git and EDA meanings were distinguished
The agent interpreted Worktree as multiple self-contained work units rather than Git worktrees. The engineer then related the intended meaning to older EDA-tool organization while recognizing how strongly the term is tied to Git (Segments 0445–0450).
The precise EDA-style umbrella label is derived from that exchange.


3. workspace became an alternative and another ambiguity
The engineer offered workspace as an alternative and asked that Cadence manuals provide another reference angle. The agent reported that both terms are overloaded and distinguished among flow, design directory, working directory, and GUI workspace in the vendor vocabulary (Segments 0452–0477).
Those vendor claims are agent reports and were not independently validated within content/session/.


4. worktree and work unit became the accepted working state
The agent proposed retaining worktree provisionally with work unit beneath it. The engineer confirmed that this pair matched the intended approach (Segments 0477–0479).
This directly supports the current working vocabulary. It does not close future naming permanently.


5. The tree later supplied an implementation view
The agent later read worktree as containing implementation units split into hardware and software, and identified UART from worktree/hardware/UART without opening its contents. The engineer used that path to demonstrate compact domain representation (Segments 0870–0896).
The reported tree state is not independently verified here.

title: Development
text: Development names a relation in which an object changes toward another state. The engineer and the agent reached the word after rejecting less stable labels, then tested it against tools, storage, and engineering work. The interaction established that its meaning depends on the object and the active context: a concept, text, implementation, workflow, or tool may be the developing object in different contexts. The working formulation of object, activity, and intended state is an agent proposal; it is not the engineer’s verbatim definition.

title: Development
text:
Scope
Development concerns an object undergoing change toward another state within CI-DIGITAL.
It is not established as a synonym for planning, authoring, software development, textual drafting, or a directory named development. Each of those may relate to it under a more specific binding.

title: Development
text:
Development through interaction

1. Development replaced an unstable authoring label
During a small-guess exercise for top-level project domains, the agent first proposed authoring, then preparation. The engineer rejected the authoring term and tested whether the activity was like planning (Segments 0582–0591).
After a web search, the agent proposed development. The engineer selected that higher-level word because its meaning could be normalized across software and non-software contexts (Segments 0592–0596).
The search sources and their wording were not preserved, so only the conversational selection supports the choice.


2. Object, activity, and intended state were proposed as qualifiers
The engineer asked what symbols or criteria had been associated with Development. The agent answered: development of what, through what activity, and toward what state (Segments 0597–0598). It then defined the object as the thing being changed or matured (Segments 0599–0600).
The engineer tested whether agents and tools were excluded. The agent answered that they are usually means but can themselves become development objects when the context changes; the engineer explicitly identified that context change (Segments 0601–0606).
The relational test is the engineer’s. The three-part qualifier and the means/object distinction are agent formulations.


3. Development separated from Storage
The engineer located the immediate inquiry in CI-DIGITAL file-tree architecture and then corrected the agent’s hierarchy. Development and Storage are sibling project domains; a development/ directory inside Storage is a representation of Development, not proof that the concept is contained by Storage (Segments 0607–0638).


4. Engineering work supplied a concrete use
The engineer described the UART controller as designed and synthesized for FPGA with AI assistance during its elaboration or Development phase (Segment 0797).
This case prevents Development from being reduced to academic writing.


5. The earlier working meaning was recalled and tested
The engineer later asked for the earlier meaning of the proposed Development folder. The agent described a working domain for drafts, notes, experiments, implementations, and intermediate outputs, excluding original inputs and final deliverables. The engineer tested whether that meant academic text, and the agent again said the object could be any artifact (Segments 0838–0841).
That inventory and its exclusions are agent reconstructions. The engineer did not explicitly adopt every item in the list.

title: AI Assistance
text: AI Assistance names the relations among AI as a project storage and work context, the assistant as one role within it, and concrete work whose relation to AI differs by purpose. The engineer framed the assistant as a highly valued tool that provides leverage toward the engineer’s goals. The interaction between the engineer and the agent then showed that discussing an AI hierarchy is not an instruction to restructure, that AI-related work should be distinguished by its object and purpose, and that a detailed software taxonomy does not belong at the top of the file tree. The title is an analytic label, not the engineer’s final taxonomy.

title: AI Assistance
text:
Scope
AI Assistance concerns AI as a project-related storage and work context, the assistant as one role within it, and concrete work whose relation to AI differs by purpose.
It does not establish a complete taxonomy of AI systems. It also does not make all AI-related artifacts one implemented pipeline, transfer authorship to an assistant, or make a tool’s capability equivalent to authority.

title: AI Assistance
text:
Development through interaction

1. Assistant and tool were rebound through the engineer’s values
The engineer first described the former authoring area as the Codex-related repository context, then clarified that the assistant is a highly important tool because it provides leverage toward the engineer’s goals. The engineer explicitly framed this as a personal understanding of tools (Segments 0741–0749).
The phrase high-leverage cognitive tool and the description of authoring as the storage face of assistance came from the agent in Segment 0748. They remain agent formulations even though they respond closely to the engineer’s account.


2. A rename request expanded into exploration and premature execution
The engineer requested changing the authoring directory to AI Assistant, then explored a broader AI parent with assistant beneath it. In the same turn, the engineer warned that not everything said was an instruction and later specified that be my assistant was the instruction (Segments 0755–0767).
The agent had already acted and proposed restoring the prior name. The engineer stopped the reversion, froze the existing state, and moved the clarified understanding forward (Segments 0767–0770). The storage idea and the instruction boundary therefore remain separate.


3. Two AI-related work units were distinguished
The engineer described OpenCode Archive Review as a historical corpus and analysis effort derived from many months of OpenCode use, and described UART as an FPGA controller designed and synthesized with AI assistance and intended as a successful AI-assisted workflow case (Segments 0790–0799).
Their common AI relation does not make their objects or artifact roles identical.


4. AI/assistant/ became a reported storage state
The engineer reported having manually established AI as a parent and assistant as its child (Segments 0806–0807). This is a reported action, not an independent verification of the present filesystem.


5. Lower-level software taxonomy was bracketed
The agent classified OpenCode and Codex as application software, agentic coding environments, agent harnesses, and developer tools. The engineer rejected that specificity for the upper-level file architecture because it was not relevant and could create more terminology and drift. The agent returned to a shallow AI storage domain whose children should appear only when material boundaries arise (Segments 0808–0812).
The detailed classifications remain agent proposals and do not govern the tree.

title: Interaction and Language Boundaries
text: Meaning and instructions must stay bounded across the surfaces through which an engineer and an AI agent interact. Through repeated corrections, the engineer distinguished language, voice, written artifacts, application interaction, local capability, repository action, and Cadence EDA terminology. The agent’s attempts to bridge these surfaces exposed where words, purposes, and rules would otherwise leak between them. The compound title is an analytic grouping rather than a phrase the engineer adopted.

title: Interaction and Language Boundaries

title: Interaction and Language Boundaries
text:
Scope
The concept concerns how meaning and instructions remain bounded across interaction surfaces and terminology contexts.
Voice rhythm is not written project text. Application interaction is not local operational capability. Repository location is not Cadence terminology. Language change is not neutral when it moves the terms through which a domain is understood.

title: Interaction and Language Boundaries
text:
Development through interaction

1. Unrequested language change was identified as drift
After the agent briefly returned to Portuguese, the engineer noted having asked for English and explained that moving material between languages can itself move terminology and meaning. The engineer requested a global English rule for this environment (Segments 0123–0140).
The agent stated a rule for new material while preserving existing source-language content until a reviewed translation is requested (Segments 0131–0140). The exact preservation wording is the agent’s, consistent with the engineer’s concern about drift.


2. Spoken rhythm and written artifacts were separated
The engineer tested whether a requested voice-only phrase would migrate into scripts, code, or Markdown, and explicitly described voice and text as boundaries to be held separately (Segments 0530–0532).


3. The agent’s inferred purpose was corrected
The agent interpreted the proposed phrase as a personal dominance cue. The engineer corrected that attribution: the phrase was a rhythm marker, and the agent’s purpose claim was not the engineer’s wording. The agent withdrew the attribution (Segments 0533–0536).
The correction concerns source and purpose. It does not require this page to reproduce or operationalize the requested phrase.


4. A surface-specific rule was proposed
The agent proposed keeping spoken rhythm markers voice-only and out of written project artifacts. The engineer asked that the relevant instruction be treated as voice-interaction guidance only, and the agent restated that it would not migrate into code, Markdown, documentation, conceptual attribution, or deliverables (Segments 0536–0542).
The comprehensive no-migration list is agent wording.


5. Voice, capability, repository action, and Cadence were rebound
The engineer corrected the agent for using cadence across voice and the Cadence EDA domain. The agent separated voice tone and delivery into application interaction, tool capability into local operation, Cadence into the EDA workflow domain, and repository control into bounded file and Git actions (Segments 0561–0563).


6. The boundary rule was accepted and generalized only to repository relevance
The engineer emphasized that not every directory in CI-DIGITAL belongs to Cadence terminology. The agent stated that location does not determine terminology and that shared words do not transfer meaning by default (Segments 0563–0565). The engineer continued with context as the active upstream frame (Segments 0566–0568).

title: Provenance
text: Provenance concerns where material came from, who contributed it, in what role, how it was transformed, and what evidential status it carries. The engineer and the agent formed several provenance rules while preserving a source corpus, attributing interpretations, and separating factual records from reconstruction and analysis. Those rules have different scopes and must not be collapsed into one general authorship rule. The central boundary, accepted by the engineer, is that what belongs to the engineer remains the engineer’s and what belongs to the agent remains the agent’s.

title: Provenance
text:
Scope
Provenance concerns the origin, speaker, role, transformation, order, and evidential status of material. It preserves differences among source text, agent interpretation, marked reconstruction, derived analysis, and later storage representation.
Provenance does not by itself prove truth, authorship beyond the stated scope, current filesystem state, or engineer adoption of a derived formulation.

title: Provenance
text:
Development through interaction

1. A source-pool authorship default became the first local boundary
The engineer described a long-lived branch as a pool containing the engineer’s prompts and other materials. For that historical pool, the engineer proposed treating Markdown and text as the engineer’s material by default, while PDFs, PDF-derived material, or material named for another person were external bibliographical references. The agent confirmed the mapping with explicit exceptions, and the engineer called it their first boundary (Segments 0178–0184).
This rule is explicitly local to that historical source pool. It must not be generalized to every Markdown file or later corpus.


2. Preservation preceded movement and mapping
The engineer changed the request from a map to a local copy of the full corpus. The agent later proposed keeping the source stable before tree movement, and the engineer directed that the archive remain the first priority (Segments 0190–0207).
The agent later reported completing that archive. Those reports are not independently verified here.


3. Intended meaning was separated from frequency
When the engineer emphasized that the larger corpus should preserve the engineer’s intended direction, the agent proposed consolidating by provenance and role rather than raw occurrence count, with the engineer’s messages as primary evidence for intended meaning (Segments 0378–0386).
That weighting rule is an agent proposal. The engineer asked what raw frequency meant but did not explicitly adopt the full method in that exchange.


4. Interpretation received an explicit attribution rule
The agent attributed an inference to the engineer. The engineer corrected it, welcomed interpretation as concept-forming work, and challenged why the agent should not label interpretation as a human would. The agent stated a symmetric rule, and the engineer accepted it as the core idea: what is the engineer’s remains the engineer’s, and what is the agent’s remains the agent’s (Segments 0504–0521).
This is the principal contribution-attribution boundary formed in the interaction.


5. Factual record, reconstruction, and analysis were separated
The engineer required a complete factual record of the exchange because compilation would lose material. When the engineer proposed filling speech gaps, the agent required the factual record to remain untouched and any gap-filling to be marked as reconstruction. The engineer explicitly praised and accepted that strategy. Derived academic analysis was placed beside, not inside, the source (Segments 0705–0718).


6. The live session displaced existing docs as the source of meaning
When the agent treated existing tree material as authority, the engineer corrected that it was only an example and said that the live session being created carried the relevant provenance. The agent then stated that session meaning should generate the classification bottom-up (Segments 0922–0947).


7. Source-bound repair exposed a coverage limit
The engineer instructed that every represented domain be checked against the source that created its meaning, so repair would not drift over earlier drift (Segment 1019).
The agent then reported that the available record did not cover earlier material and began explaining that the lineage frame had come from the conversation (Segments 1023–1026). That coverage mismatch was later resolved for the recorded interval. Evidence outside that interval and the authorship of the derived lineage remain unresolved.

title: Temporal Axis
text: Temporal Axis describes how a developing understanding relates prior conceptual state, present correction, retained history, and forward application. It emerged when an engineer stopped an AI agent from reversing a premature change and instead required the newly clarified understanding to govern what followed. The term churn was then adopted for repeated change that adds no material correction.

title: Temporal Axis
text: Temporal Axis describes how a developing understanding relates prior conceptual state, present correction, retained history, and forward application. It emerged when an engineer stopped an AI agent from reversing a premature change and instead required the newly clarified understanding to govern what followed. The term churn was then adopted for repeated change that adds no material correction.

title: Temporal Axis
text:
Scope
The concept applies to conceptual and repository evolution where previous states remain relevant to present decisions. It does not prohibit correction, make accidental changes correct, or require preservation of a harmful contradiction.

title: Temporal Axis
text:
Development through interaction

1. Premature execution prompted a proposed reversion
During exploration of an AI parent domain, the agent proceeded before the broader structure had been established and then proposed restoring the earlier state. The engineer stopped that reversion. — Segments 0762–0770.


2. The present state was retained
The engineer required the existing result to remain, the clarified rule to be established at the current point, and future changes to follow from there: do not revert; freeze the current state. — Segments 0768–0772.


3. Forward application was formulated
The agent expressed the rule as preserving what happened, establishing the new understanding, applying it forward, and returning to earlier states only when they materially conflict. The engineer accepted that direction. — Segments 0773–0776.


4. Necessary correction was kept possible
The engineer observed that reversing a change likely to be repeated merely duplicates effort. The agent qualified the rule: contradiction or harm can still justify retrospective correction; otherwise the process should move forward without churn. — Segments 0778–0779.


5. Churn became the adopted term
The agent introduced churn for unnecessary repeated change, and the engineer explicitly adopted it. — Segments 0779–0780.


6. The relevant predecessor became conceptual, not merely sequential
Later development separated the last applicable conceptual knowledge state from the immediately preceding turn. Intervening events may belong to other contexts and therefore need not be conceptual predecessors. A later understanding must recover the relevant prior state, not merely the nearest event in time.

title: Temporal Axis
text:
Current formulation

Preserve the actual history of development rather than rewriting it as though a later rule had always governed.
Establish a clarified understanding at the point where it becomes available.
Apply that understanding forward.
Revisit an earlier state when a material conflict, contradiction, or harm requires correction.
Treat unnecessary reversal and repetition as churn.
Identify conceptual predecessors by relevance to the active context, not by temporal adjacency alone.
Preserve enough of a correction to explain what changed, why it changed, and what can now be carried forward.

A compact transition is:
relevant prior state -> present situation -> interpretation -> observable mismatch -> correction -> resulting state

Detection alone does not require reversion.


Concept Lineage Method
Retains corrections without rewriting prior stages.
Lineage describes development; it does not excuse inconsistency.


Simplicity
Avoiding churn conserves effort and attention.
Simplicity does not block necessary migration.


Development
State transitions make development observable over time.
No universal lifecycle model is claimed.

Modeling unit
The graph models a concept state, not a glossary term.
A concept state is one materially distinct point in a concept’s temporal lineage. A concept can therefore have several nodes: emergence, interpretation, correction, contextual rebinding, accepted working meaning, and unresolved branch.
Nodes do not collapse user statements, assistant interpretations, corrections, and acceptance into one timeless claim. Edges preserve how one state leads to another.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Root object
The JSON root contains:

schema_version: Version of this repository-local model.
artifact_id: Stable identifier for the graph artifact.
status: Must remain candidate until an explicit validation and promotion decision.
title: Human-readable description.
source: Controlling transcript and evidence boundary.
derivation: Method and authority limits.
status_registry: Allowed node statuses.
relation_type_registry: Allowed and documented edge meanings.
nodes: Concept-state nodes.
edges: Typed temporal and cross-concept relations.
uncertainties: Known limits that must survive later validation.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Node schema
Every node requires these fields:








Field
Type
Meaning




id
string
Stable, unique identifier. The identifier persists if wording is refined.


concept
string
Concept lineage to which the state belongs.


state_summary
string
Concise attributed summary of the state or claim.


lineage_position
string
Descriptive position such as emergence, correction, current working rule, or open branch. It is not an authority status.


source_segment_anchors
non-empty array
Exact transcript anchors supporting the state.


speaker
string
Primary attributed speaker: user, assistant, or mixed.


attribution
string
Explanation of who originated, interpreted, corrected, or accepted the state.


status
enum
Evidence and adoption status defined below.


call_order
object
First and last call, segment, and source ordinal covered by the state.



Each node source anchor contains:

call: Call number.
segment: Zero-padded transcript segment identifier.
source_ordinal: Original source ordinal.
role: Recorded transcript role.
function: Evidentiary function such as definition, correction, proposal, or explicit_acceptance.

call_order contains first_call, first_segment, first_source_ordinal, last_call, last_segment, and last_source_ordinal. These values support deterministic temporal sorting without replacing the exact source anchors.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Node status semantics
The allowed statuses are intentionally narrow:

attested: Directly present in the transcript and attributed to its speaker. It does not imply universal truth or final adoption.
assistant-proposed: An assistant formulation or taxonomy without direct user acceptance in the captured evidence.
user-corrected: The user explicitly corrected, narrowed, or rebound a preceding formulation. The node summary follows that correction.
user-accepted: An assistant or mixed formulation with direct user acceptance in a cited user segment. Every such node must contain a user anchor whose function begins with explicit_acceptance.
unresolved: The transcript leaves a conflict, incomplete explanation, missing validation, or open branch.

Polite acknowledgements are not automatically acceptance. Acceptance is used only when the local exchange directly treats the formulation as correct, governing, or the basis for continuation.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Edge schema
Every edge requires:








Field
Type
Meaning




id
string
Unique stable edge identifier.


from
string
Existing source node identifier.


to
string
Existing target node identifier.


relation
enum
A relation documented in relation_type_registry.


source_segment_anchors
non-empty array
Transcript evidence for the transition or cross-concept relation.


attribution
string
Who made or supports the relation and what must not be inferred from it.



The graph currently uses these relation types:

emerged_from: The target becomes a distinct concept state through the source episode.
interpreted_as: The target is an attributed interpretation of the source.
corrected_by: The source is explicitly corrected or narrowed by the target.
rebound_in_context: The concept or relation receives a new context-specific binding.
derived_from: The target follows analytically without claiming identity.
explicitly_accepted: The target is directly accepted by the user at a cited segment.
remains_unresolved: The target preserves an open or conflicting branch.
represented_as: One domain or concept is expressed in another representation, such as a domain represented by a directory.
constrained_by: The target bounds the valid scope of the source.
motivates: The source supplies the reason for the target.
distinguished_from: The target is explicitly separated from the source.
governs: The source supplies operative interpretation or production rules for the target.

Relation direction is semantically significant. For example, A corrected_by B means B is the corrected state, and A represented_as B means B is the representation.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Uncertainty schema
Every uncertainty requires:

id: Unique uncertainty identifier.
summary: What is not settled.
source_segment_anchors: Evidence that the limit exists.
impact: What later work must not infer until the uncertainty is resolved.

Uncertainties are part of the model, not validation noise. Promotion must not delete them merely to obtain a cleaner graph.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Structural invariants
A valid candidate graph must satisfy all of the following:

The JSON parses successfully.
Node, edge, and uncertainty identifiers are unique in their own collections.
Every node contains all required fields and at least one source anchor.
Every edge references existing nodes and uses a documented relation type.
Every source anchor resolves to a segment in the controlling transcript with the same call and source ordinal.
Every node status belongs to status_registry.
Every user-accepted node contains a direct user acceptance anchor.
Node call/order bounds match the first and last source anchors.
No structural cycle is automatically treated as an error. Conceptual rebinding can legitimately revisit an earlier concept; temporal order remains in source anchors.
status remains candidate until semantic validation is complete.

title: Candidate concept-lineage graph schema
text:
Semantic validation and promotion gate
Structural validity is necessary but not sufficient. Before any promotion, an independent review must:

Compare every node summary with all cited transcript segments.
Check that omitted nearby segments do not reverse or materially narrow the summary.
Confirm attribution, especially user-accepted and user-corrected states.
Check each edge direction and relation type against conversational order.
Resolve or explicitly retain each uncertainty.
Compare existing concept Markdown files against the validated graph and report discrepancies without allowing those files to retroactively change transcript-derived evidence.
Obtain an explicit decision to designate a validated revision as the golden model.

Until all gates pass, downstream comparison may identify differences, but the candidate graph must not be used to overwrite domain files.

title: Conceptual Provenance
text: Conceptual Provenance names the trace from present reasoning to previously formed, bounded, and recorded conceptual structures that provide its foundation. The engineer established the core meaning during the interaction: recorded concepts work like memory, and their later influence works like experience. The agent organized that meaning into a compact relation model that the engineer accepted as a useful representation. The term is a current shared symbol, not a final definition.

title: Conceptual Provenance
text: Conceptual Provenance names the trace from present reasoning to previously formed, bounded, and recorded conceptual structures that provide its foundation. The engineer established the core meaning during the interaction: recorded concepts work like memory, and their later influence works like experience. The agent organized that meaning into a compact relation model that the engineer accepted as a useful representation. The term is a current shared symbol, not a final definition.

title: Conceptual Provenance
text:
Scope
Conceptual Provenance concerns how prior elaboration, once bounded and recorded, becomes available as a foundation for later reasoning, and how that foundation keeps its attribution and context.
It is not limited to bibliography. Bibliographical references may support a concept, but the concept’s provenance also includes the prior contexts, distinctions, relations, corrections, and recordings through which its usable meaning developed. It does not merge Provenance, Ontology, Memory, Experience, or Reasoning into one concept.

title: Conceptual Provenance
text:
Development through interaction

1. The engineer established the core meaning
The engineer described present reasoning as founded on previously formed and recorded conceptual structures. In the human analogy, a recorded conceptual structure functions as memory, and its later influence on perception, modeling, and action functions as experience in another sense.


2. The agent proposed a compact relation model
The agent organized the meaning as a chain:
past elaboration -> bounded conceptual structure -> recorded state -> later retrieval -> foundation for new reasoning
The engineer accepted this organization as a useful representation of the meaning. The chain and the page’s organization remain agent formulations.


3. Adjacent concepts were kept separate
The concept was distinguished from:

Provenance, which traces the origin and transformation of claims, artifacts, and observations in its own context;
Ontology, which concerns the entities and relations that can carry meaning within a domain;
Memory, which is the persistence and later availability of a recorded conceptual structure;
Experience, which is the later use or influence of prior conceptual structures; and
Reasoning, which can use those structures to form candidate domains, intentions, and relations.

Conceptual provenance records their relevant relations without making them identical or creating an unsupported interface.


4. Reuse during exploration was bounded by attribution
When the agent encounters a new or poorly defined domain, it may retrieve prior recorded concepts and use them within its own bounded conceptual-exploration domain. A reused suggestion or concept keeps its original attribution and context through a derived from relation. A new agent formulation remains agent-derived and does not alter the engineer’s original meaning.


5. Recording and reopening were made explicit
Conceptual structures that become sufficiently formed and bounded should be recorded so they can provide observable foundations for later reasoning. Candidates may remain open while recorded, with their status, attribution, and relations explicit. If the term later collides with another concept or domain, that collision is a signal to reopen epistemological analysis, inspect the provenance, refine the boundaries, and append the resulting understanding without erasing earlier states.

title: Symbol and Binding
text: Symbol and Binding developed through the engineer–agent interaction as the relation by which words, names, paths, and other representations acquire context-specific meaning. The concept was tested through terminology collisions, unnecessary cross-context reminders, shared understanding, and file-tree navigation (Segments 0561–0896).

title: Symbol and Binding
text: Symbol and Binding developed through the engineer–agent interaction as the relation by which words, names, paths, and other representations acquire context-specific meaning. The concept was tested through terminology collisions, unnecessary cross-context reminders, shared understanding, and file-tree navigation (Segments 0561–0896).

title: Symbol and Binding
text:
Scope
This concept includes symbols, semantic relations, contextual bindings, their stabilization, and their realignment across contexts.
It does not establish one formal semiotic, linguistic, programming-language, or information-theoretic definition of binding. Binding remains a project-adapted relation term whose specific kind must be inferred or stated from context.

title: Symbol and Binding
text:
Development through interaction

1. Shared words exposed context-specific meaning
The engineer corrected the transfer of terminology among voice interaction, Codex capability, Cadence EDA, and repository control. The correction established that a shared surface word does not carry one meaning across domains (Segments 0561–0568).


2. Unnecessary material created a binding without an interface
The engineer observed that restating unrelated material creates an overlay or binding where no interface exists. The agent named the event context leakage through a spurious binding. The behavior rule was adopted, while the phrase remains agent-origin (Segments 0611–0620).


3. Symbols and bindings became possible domain entities
The engineer proposed that entities may be symbols and that sets of symbols, bindings, semantic relations, and ontologies can themselves participate in domains (Segments 0646–0648).


4. Normalized relations supported shared meaning
The engineer described reasoning as organizing relations among symbols. When semantics and relations become normalized between entities and participants, a symbol can carry shared meaning (Segments 0687–0689).
The ZIP-file comparison expressed semantic density. The agent introduced semantic compression as a candidate term; it was not established as engineer wording (Segments 0689–0691).


5. Realignment enabled context return
After conceptual expansion, the engineer observed that bindings or symbols could be realigned to return quickly to the file-tree context (Segments 0731–0736).


6. The file tree became a compact symbol
The engineer described a path as a representation of a denser domain, allowing details to remain unopened until needed. The tree therefore carries compact contextual meaning without replacing deeper content (Segments 0884–0896).

title: Symbol and Binding
text:
Current formulation

A symbol is a representational carrier whose active meaning depends on context and relations.
Binding is a project-adapted term for a relation that connects a symbol, entity, meaning, or cross-domain correspondence.
Shared terminology does not transfer one binding across domains automatically.
A relation introduced without a relevant interface can produce context leakage.
Organized and normalized relations support shared meaning.
Active bindings can be realigned when the interaction returns to an earlier context.
A file path can symbolize a denser domain and support on-demand access.

title: Ontology
text: Ontology emerged through the engineer–agent interaction as the organization of entity kinds, relation kinds, and conditions under which domains and interfaces become intelligible. It was first explored conceptually and later tested through a concrete session instruction treated as the ontology of its bounded domain (Segments 0646–0686 and 0979–0988).

title: Ontology
text: Ontology emerged through the engineer–agent interaction as the organization of entity kinds, relation kinds, and conditions under which domains and interfaces become intelligible. It was first explored conceptually and later tested through a concrete session instruction treated as the ontology of its bounded domain (Segments 0646–0686 and 0979–0988).

title: Ontology
text:
Scope
Ontology includes explicit distinctions among entities, relations, domains, and admissible connections for a stated domain.
It does not yet establish whether ontology is discovered, constructed, specified, or co-produced through inquiry. It is not a final metaphysical inventory, a complete interface test, or an implemented ontology language.

title: Ontology
text:
Development through interaction

1. Ontology appeared as a higher-order entity
The engineer included ontologies among the entities that could themselves be grouped into domains and sought the information architecture beneath labels (Segments 0646–0648).


2. Ontology became related to interface and overlap
While distinguishing interface from unresolved overlap, the engineer said that ontology “said” or set the interface and connected the issue to the kinds of entities and relations present (Segments 0673–0677).
The agent strengthened this into the claim that ontology determines allowed entities and relations and thereby constrains interfaces. That modal account is an agent formulation (Segment 0681).


3. Knowing was said to create ontology
The engineer connected knowing with recognizing domains, relations, and entity kinds, from which architecture can develop bottom-up while top-down abstraction remains possible (Segment 0682).
The agent described ontology as the “current best expression.” The engineer adopted non-finality for the wider inquiry, but not that exact formulation as personal wording (Segments 0684–0686).


4. A session instruction became a working ontology
The engineer identified the scoped session instruction as the ontology of that domain. The agent explained that it defines what exists, which relations are valid, and how interaction becomes structured content; the engineer accepted that explanation (Segments 0979–0988).
This is a domain-specific use. File type alone does not make every instruction file an ontology.

title: Ontology
text:
Current formulation

Ontology organizes the entities and relations through which a domain is made explicit.
It participates in determining which cross-domain relations can become intelligible interfaces.
Knowing develops the conceptual distinctions from which an ontology can be expressed.
Ontology remains revisable as understanding develops.
A governing instruction can function as a working ontology when it explicitly establishes the entities, relations, and constraints of its domain.
No general rule makes every instruction artifact an ontology.

title: Context
text: Context emerged through engineer–agent correction as the active runtime of meaning: the frame that determines which entities, symbols, relations, terminology, goals, and actions are relevant now. The concept was tested whenever the interaction changed domains or imported an unrelated qualification (Segments 0559–0638).

title: Context
text: Context emerged through engineer–agent correction as the active runtime of meaning: the frame that determines which entities, symbols, relations, terminology, goals, and actions are relevant now. The concept was tested whenever the interaction changed domains or imported an unrelated qualification (Segments 0559–0638).

title: Context
text:
Scope
Context includes the active domain, purpose, relations, evidence, and constraints governing interpretation.
It is not equivalent to a directory, tool capability, all available information, or a timeless definition. Inactive material remains available but does not participate until a relevant relation requires it.

title: Context
text:
Development through interaction

1. Operational layers exposed different contexts
The engineer separated local-computer operation, the Codex application, repository work, voice interaction, tool capability, and Cadence terminology. Corrections showed that proximity does not make their meanings interchangeable (Segments 0559–0568).


2. Context became the runtime of meaning
After the agent offered a broad definition, the engineer refined it through worktree: selecting that context activates its internal references and leaves unrelated material outside the present focus. The engineer called this the “runtime of meaning” (Segments 0570–0573).
The agent introduced bracketing for material left inactive rather than erased. This is an agent formulation of the engineer’s distinction.


3. A floating context list failed
The agent proposed a generic context taxonomy. The engineer rejected it because it was not anchored to the domains being developed through the file tree. The correction established incremental, object-bound context discovery (Segments 0574–0584).


4. Unnecessary qualification exposed leakage
The engineer identified an unrelated qualification as a new binding without an interface and stopped the drift. The agent named this context leakage through a spurious binding. The engineer adopted the behavior rule for later work without explicitly adopting the phrase as personal wording (Segments 0611–0620).


5. Contexts became nested and movable
The engineer distinguished the CI-DIGITAL project from narrower contexts such as Storage and Development, corrected their sibling relation, and explained how one underlying object may appear differently under changed context (Segments 0621–0638).
After a conceptual parenthesis, the engineer returned to file-tree architecture by realigning symbols and bindings. Context therefore supported controlled movement without importing the full contents of every prior domain (Segments 0731–0736).


6. Context separated exploration from execution
The engineer described point of view as an angle on a context or domain and distinguished imaginative modeling from action in the world. The agent formulated this as a conceptual sandbox with an exploration–execution boundary (Segments 0828–0835).


7. Context bounded later concept extraction
The engineer later established content/session/ as the context for extracting the session’s concepts and prohibited movement beyond that boundary. This made Context both a subject of study and the means by which the study’s scope was controlled (Segments 0943–0997).

title: Context
text:
Current formulation

Context is the active runtime of meaning.
It selects which domain, terminology, relations, evidence, and actions presently participate.
Contexts can be nested without collapsing sibling domains.
One object can have different contextual representations.
Inactive material remains available but requires a relevant relation before entering.
Unnecessary import creates contextual drift; the project term for that event is context leakage through a spurious binding.
Context can govern both conceptual inquiry and repository action while keeping exploration distinct from execution.
