For non-plain-text sources, run a generic derivation with an extraction/parser/OCR specialization and preserve versioned inputs, tools/configuration/environment, page/span map, output identity/hash, quality, and uncertainty.
Segment by message, quotation, code block, document structure, and candidate language boundaries while preserving reversible locators.
Apply deterministic language decisions and segment-level VLSI applicability/admission rules; source- or container-level scope remains routing metadata only.
Preserve raw/extracted text versions and reversible span locators.
Apply a versioned, reversible normalization view.
Tokenize and sentence-segment with a pinned implementation and ruleset.
Produce token, lemma, and contiguous n-gram occurrences.
Aggregate by provenance class, source, authenticated session, interaction group, and time window.
Generate co-occurrence observations under named window definitions.
Generate candidates; do not assign semantic relation types automatically.

Every output-producing step creates a derivation_run and registered output artifact_version; a combined procedure may emit several outputs, but each output retains the same valid producing-run FK and its own identity/hash. A derived table cannot use a free-form run label in place of that FK.
Language detection software may nominate segments for review, but corpus inclusion is deterministic with respect to the stored decision record. A probabilistic language score is never silently converted into a permanent English/non-English fact.


7.2 Reversible normalization
Normalization produces a derived view and never overwrites raw_text. Each normalized token retains its source span and the sequence of applied rules. Rules may include Unicode normalization, whitespace normalization, case-folding for a comparison view, punctuation handling, and a domain-specific protected-token list for forms such as SystemVerilog, UVM, RTL, 3D-IC, IEEE 1800.2, signal names, and HDL operators.
Lemmatization and stemming are analyses, not corrections. Both should retain the surface form. Acronym expansion is an annotation relation (abbreviation_of or expanded_as_in_source), not a normalization that destroys the acronym.


7.3 Measures and their evidence basis








Measure
Definition
Evidence basis and limitation




TF(t,p)
Occurrences of term t in provenance class p.
Token occurrences under one tokenizer/normalizer configuration. It measures recurrence, not importance.


DF(t)
Count of distinct authenticated source versions containing t.
source_version_id; revisions are distinct versions, while mirrors and derivatives must not inflate the count. DF is not evidence independence.


ISF(x,c,r)
Independent-source frequency: count of evidence-lineage equivalence classes supporting item x for claim/analysis scope c under named independence rule r.
Rule r collapses revisions, mirrors, quotations, derivatives, and common underlying evidence; unknown independence is reported separately and not counted.


SF(t)
Count of authenticated sessions containing t.
Only non-null source-native session_id. Otherwise unavailable, never substituted by dates.


IGF(t)
Count of local interaction groups containing t.
Named grouping rule and version; reported separately from SF.


UF/AF(t)
User-only and assistant-only occurrences.
origin_actor; quoted spans excluded from the quoting actor.


first_seen/last_seen
Earliest/latest supported time interval.
Time value plus precision and uncertainty.


persistence_span
Interval between supported first and last observation bounds.
Not meaningful as activity continuity; long spans may contain no intermediate use.


window_frequency
Occurrences or documents per declared calendar or release window.
Fixed window definition and complete-enough acquisition scope.


cooccurrence_count(a,b,w)
Number of distinct windows w containing both items.
Exact window type, source set, and item spans. It is an observational edge only.


provenance_balance(t)
Vector of counts by origin/content role.
Detects assistant, quotation, file, or tool dominance; not a quality score.


support_set(c)
Unique evidence IDs linked to claim c.
Identity-preserving set; projected and duplicate evidence remain marked.



No composite number is called “confidence.” If a future pilot needs ranking, it may compute a versioned support index from declared inputs, but the record must state that the index is ordinal or heuristic, not a probability. Its formula, calibration set, sensitivity analysis, and limitations are configuration items. A formula-only change cannot alter support_set, ISF, or claim/release eligibility.


7.4 Corpus adequacy and temporal claims
Counts are always reportable, but recurrence and trend claims require adequacy gates. For the future pilot:

a phrase is “observed” after one occurrence and “recurrent” only under a declared minimum count and source-dispersion rule;
no trend direction is issued with fewer than three complete comparison windows;
a change is reported with raw window counts and acquisition coverage, not only a percentage;
sparse or censored windows are labeled insufficient rather than interpolated; and
a source added late to the archive is distinguished from language first used late in the underlying work.

Thresholds are project acceptance parameters, not universal statistical facts. They must be justified against corpus size, retrieval use, false-positive cost, and reviewer capacity.


7.5 Candidate relation generation
Candidate generation may use co-occurrence, lexical similarity, shared source distributions, repeated syntactic patterns, temporal alignment, and model suggestions. Each candidate stores every contributing signal independently. A model may propose depends_on, measures, or implements; the system records that proposal, model/configuration, prompt/input IDs, and rationale in an immutable candidate record. An accepted review may support creation of a separate semantic claim with a new identifier; it never changes the candidate edge into a semantic edge.
A projected concept-to-domain edge is always a derived analytical observation in observation_graph. Projection may summarize accepted or observed lower-level assignments, but it may never masquerade as a semantic domain assertion, enter reviewed_semantic_graph, or increase independent support. If a semantic concept-to-domain relation is needed, it is created as a separate claim with its own identifier, predicate, segment-level VLSI applicability, admissible evidence, counterevidence review, and disposition.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
text:
9. Standards-by-concern matrix
Status was checked against official records on 9 September 2026. Standards are complementary concerns, not a maturity ladder.



Concern
Baseline and status
Role in CI-DIGITAL
Explicit non-role




Terminology principles
ISO 704:2022, published
Concept/definition/designation discipline; term formation and concept-system work.
Does not define CI-DIGITAL’s VLSI concepts or graph storage.


Terminology vocabulary
ISO 1087:2019, confirmed 2025
Shared terminology-work vocabulary.
Explicitly does not cover computer-application-specific terminology work; no pipeline architecture.


Controlled vocabularies
ANSI/NISO Z39.19-2005 (R2010), withdrawn in 2020
Historical guidance on warrant, candidate terms, term records, semantic relationships, testing, maintenance, and retrieval evaluation.27
Not current, not an ontology language, and not VLSI domain authority.


Thesaurus construction/exchange
ISO 25964-1:2011, published, revision underway
Thesaurus scope, relationships, management, data model, and exchange principles.
Not a database/search-engine specification; not identical to SKOS.


Vocabulary interoperability
ISO 25964-2:2013, confirmed 2023, revision initiated 2026
Mapping architecture and maintenance across vocabularies.
Does not authorize silent merge or equivalence.


Harmonization
ISO 860:2007, confirmed 2021
Method for deliberate harmonization of concepts, systems, definitions, and terms.
Not the default for independently governed sources.


Knowledge organization representation
W3C SKOS, Recommendation 2009
RDF representation of KOS concepts, labels, notes, semantic links, and mappings.
Co-occurrence is not skos:related; membership is not hierarchy.


Graph data model
W3C RDF 1.1, Recommendation 2014; RDF 1.2 Candidate Recommendation Snapshot 2026
Stable graph representation baseline; named graphs/datasets can separate provenance contexts.
RDF triples alone are not an ontology, truth guarantee, or closed validation schema.


Formal ontology
W3C OWL 2, Recommendation 2012
Formal classes, properties, axioms, inference, and consistency where justified.
A reasoner does not validate source meaning or intended use.


Graph constraints
W3C SHACL, Recommendation 2017
Structural/profile checks and detailed validation reports for RDF graphs.
A conforming graph can still contain semantically wrong assertions.


Provenance
W3C PROV-DM/PROV-O, Recommendations 2013
Interchange model for entities, activities, agents, derivation, attribution, and responsibility.
Does not authenticate a source or determine trust automatically.


Architecture description
ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022, published
Stakeholder/concern/viewpoint discipline and separation of architecture from descriptions.
Does not prescribe the corpus method, notation, tool, or renderer.


Measurement
ISO/IEC/IEEE 15939:2017, published, revision underway
Tie measures to information needs, definitions, analysis, use, and evaluation.
Does not justify arbitrary composite confidence scores.


Configuration management
ISO 10007:2017, confirmed 2023, revision underway
Planning, configuration identification, change control, status accounting, and audit across concept-to-retirement.
Git history alone is not complete configuration management.


Lifecycle processes
ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023, published
Lifecycle framing, recursive/iterative processes, verification, validation, and retirement.
Does not prescribe one lifecycle model or information format.


Assurance concepts
ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-1:2025, published
Shared assurance concepts and relationship among claims, argumentation, and evidence.
Does not specify how to measure each property.


Assurance cases
ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022, published
Structure and maintenance requirements for assurance cases.
Does not make every concept-graph release require a safety case.


V&V
IEEE 1012-2024, active, published 2025
V&V processes across systems, software, hardware, interfaces, documentation, and lifecycle products.28
Testing alone is not all V&V; a pass does not imply intended-use validation.


Semiconductor terminology
IEC 60050-521:2002, horizontal standard
Primary domain terminology source for semiconductor devices and integrated circuits.
Does not define project-specific workflow or evidence relations.


HDL/design/verification language
IEEE 1800-2023, active
Authoritative SystemVerilog syntax and semantics, including design, assertions, coverage, and testbenches.
Language membership does not establish project importance.


Verification methodology
IEEE 1800.2-2020, active; IEEE/IEC 62530-2-2023 adoption
UVM language-reference concepts and interoperability context.
A UVM class hierarchy is not the concept-graph hierarchy.


Coverage exchange
Accellera UCIS 1.0
Coverage-data interoperability and provenance-aware merge lessons.
Coverage metrics are not evidence of semantic completeness by themselves.


IC test access
IEEE 1500-2022; IEEE 1838-2019; IEEE 1687-2014 inactive-reserved; P1687 active revision project
Domain anchors for embedded cores, stacked dies, and embedded instrumentation.29
The published 1687-2014 status and the P1687 project status are distinct; these remain scoped test architectures, not a universal DFT taxonomy.


Industry vocabularies/data models
SEMI terms; Si2/OpenAccess, LEF/DEF, and Si2 AI-for-EDA ontology
Candidate external authorities and mappings for manufacturing/design data.
Not automatically normative for CI-DIGITAL; preserve source scheme and version.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
text:
10. Evidence, claims, assurance, and traceability

10.1 Evidence classes are not claim statuses
Evidence describes what kind of support exists. Record-family state describes where an observation, candidate, claim version, release association, or governed item sits in its own lifecycle. These dimensions must not share one field, and one record family never changes into another.








Evidence class
Meaning
Typical example




E-SOURCE
Authenticated primary corpus material
Original user message export, HDL file at a commit, standard record, signed test report.


E-DERIVED
Reproducible result from a declared procedure
Token occurrence, normalized view, TF/DF table, co-occurrence window.


E-DOMAIN
Authoritative external VLSI/EDA definition or requirement
Applicable IEC/IEEE/Accellera clause with exact locator and scheme version.


E-PROJECT
Versioned CI-DIGITAL project requirement or domain specification
Approved requirement baseline that states the applicable artifact, activity, intended use, or relation.


E-ANNOTATION
Human, rule-based, or model semantic interpretation
Proposed concept boundary or relation type with rationale.


E-REVIEW
Recorded subject-matter review or adjudication
Accepted definition, rejected mapping, counterexample disposition.


E-CHECK
Result of a defined verification or validation procedure
Reproducibility test, SHACL report, retrieval trial, reviewer agreement study.


E-DECISION
Authorized governance action
Approval for release, deprecation, waiver, or retirement.











Record/view state
Meaning
Allowed exposure




observation:recorded
An immutable observation is directly present or deterministically measured.
Observation views and audit records.


candidate:open
A separate candidate record has been nominated for semantic review.
Curator workspace; clearly marked in exploratory UI.


claim:proposed
A separate claim version and evidence package have been prepared.
Review package only.


claim:reviewed-accepted
A review record accepted the claim version for a stated use.
Pre-release validation and integration tests.


claim:reviewed-rejected
A review record rejected the claim version with rationale/counterevidence.
Governance history; excluded from active semantic view.


release:published
Derived view: an accepted claim version is associated with an identified release by a successful publication event.
Production retrieval and export within approved use.


item:deprecated
A separate deprecation record limits new assignment while retaining history/retrieval.
Published with replacement and validity interval.


item:retired
A separate retirement decision removes the item from active use after impact handling.
Historical registry only.



A claim version may appear in a published-release view while supported by mixed evidence classes. Conversely, an E-CHECK item may record a failed procedure and therefore support rejection rather than publication. Observation, candidate, claim, decision, and event identifiers remain distinct throughout.


10.2 Enforceable evidence profiles by claim type
Each claim_type references a versioned evidence-admissibility profile. Evidence links carry a role such as corpus_warrant, domain_support, project_support, counterevidence, review_input, verification_result, or validation_result; an untyped bag of attachments is insufficient. Release gates evaluate required roles and independent lineage groups, not merely the number of linked records.








Claim type
Minimum admissible profile
Evidence that cannot satisfy the minimum by itself




Lexical observation
Reproducible E-DERIVED item linked to exact occurrences and source versions.
Annotation, review, approval, or publication records.


Term/designation claim
At least one exact corpus occurrence plus applicable E-DOMAIN or E-PROJECT warrant for use as a VLSI designation.
Frequency, preferred-label vote, or curator preference alone.


Concept definition or cid: membership
Applicable E-DOMAIN evidence or a versioned E-PROJECT requirement, with segment-level VLSI applicability and scope/counterexample review.
E-ANNOTATION, E-REVIEW, and E-DECISION, singly or together.


Semantic relation
Applicable E-DOMAIN evidence or a versioned E-PROJECT requirement that directly supports the stated predicate and endpoints; at least one accepted semantic review.
Co-occurrence, projection, model rationale, annotation, review, or approval without qualifying domain/project support.


Cross-scheme mapping
Identified definitions and versions from both schemes, intended/prohibited use, comparison rationale, and mapping review.
Shared labels, shared notation, or one scheme’s assertion alone.


Release-fitness claim
Passing required verification records plus current validation records for every approved intended use and limitation.
Governance approval without check and intended-use evidence.


Deprecation or retirement claim
Versioned change request, dependency/impact analysis, migration or no-replacement rationale, and authorized decision.
Age, low frequency, or a replacement label alone.



The minimum is enforced through claim_type_profiles, typed claim_evidence_links, foreign keys, and release-gate queries. E-ANNOTATION, E-REVIEW, and E-DECISION remain valuable evidence of interpretation and governance, but they cannot circularly create domain support. For concept definitions and semantic relations, the gate requires at least one qualifying E-DOMAIN or E-PROJECT item whose lineage is not the annotation, review, or approval package itself. Mixed evidence classes remain visible; governance evidence supplements rather than substitutes for VLSI-domain or project support.


10.3 Claim record
Every semantic claim should contain:
claim_id
claim_type
subject_id
predicate_id
object_or_value
scope_scheme_id
asserted_by
assertion_method
asserted_at
claim_type_profile_id
claim_evidence_link_ids[]
claim_dependency_link_ids[]
intended_use_link_ids[]
review_ids[]
verification_record_ids[]
validation_record_ids[]
valid_from / valid_to
supersedes_claim_id
Any current claim state shown in a query is derived from immutable review, claim-state, deprecation, retirement, approval, and publication records; it is not a mutable field in the canonical claims table. An observation nominates a separate candidate, review records support a separate claim, approval is a separate decision, and publication is a separate event/release association.
The claim text must be atomic enough to test. “The graph is valid” is not atomic. Better claims are: “every published concept in release R has exactly one English preferred label under profile P”; “relation R12 is supported by IEEE 1800-2023, Clause X”; or “query set Q achieves the approved recall threshold against relevance judgments J.” Approval and publication are not fields owned by the claim. Independent approval_decisions, release_items, and publication_events reference claims and release candidates. A claim’s published status is therefore a release-derived view that exists only after an accepted decision and a successful publication event.


10.4 Source-to-claim traceability
Traceability is many-to-many and typed:





flowchart LR
    S[Source version] -->|contains| G[Segment]
    G -->|grounds| E[Evidence item and lineage]
    E -->|yields under procedure| O[Observation]
    O -->|nominates| C[Candidate]
    A[Qualifying domain or project evidence] -->|supports or conflicts| P[Semantic claim]
    C -->|review supports separate| P
    P -->|checked by| V[Verification record]
    P -->|evaluated for use by| U[Validation record]
    P --> RC[Release candidate]
    V --> D[Independent approval decision]
    U --> D
    RC --> D
    D --> PE[Publication event]
    PE --> R[Published release association]






An edge is not adequately traceable because it carries a source count. Its evidence links must resolve to exact source versions, spans, evidence items, and lineage groups. Where one domain edge is a projection of a concept edge, the derivation is represented directly; the original evidence is not copied and recounted. The projection remains an analytical observation. A reviewed semantic domain assertion, if needed, is a different claim and must satisfy its evidence profile independently.


10.5 Assurance argument
ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-1:2025 defines the shared vocabulary and concepts for assurance, while Part 2 specifies assurance-case structure and meaning.3031 The index does not need a maximal assurance case for every edit, but a release should have an inspectable argument:

Top claim: Release R is fit for approved uses U under limitations L.
Subclaim A — evidence integrity: sources are authenticated to the stated level, provenance classes are separated, and derivations are reproducible.
Subclaim B — semantic integrity: concepts and relations are supported by scoped VLSI authorities and reviewed counterexamples.
Subclaim C — representation integrity: records satisfy the release schema/shape and expected logical consequences.
Subclaim D — retrieval utility: representative CI-DIGITAL tasks meet agreed performance and usability criteria.
Subclaim E — change control: configuration items, baselines, impact analysis, and required re-verification and/or re-validation obligations are complete.

Each subclaim links to evidence and recorded limitations. A failed or missing subclaim is visible; it cannot be hidden behind verified=true.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
text:
11. Verification and validation matrix
IEEE 1012-2024 applies V&V across systems, software, hardware, interfaces, information, and documentation, and includes analysis, review, inspection, assessment, and testing.32 SEBoK similarly treats verification as lifecycle-wide and identifies verification plans, matrices, procedures, tools, configurations, expected results, observed results, nonconformances, and change requests.33 This methodology uses the following separate acceptance questions:











Question
Object
Reference/baseline
Method
Result type
What it does not prove




Source authentication
Source version
Export, hash, DOI/standard record, repository commit
Hash comparison, identifier resolution, provenance inspection
Authenticated, partially authenticated, unavailable
That source statements are correct.


Transformation reproducibility
Derived artifact
Input set + procedure/configuration baseline
Clean rerun and hash/table comparison
Equal/different with diagnostic
That the rules are semantically appropriate.


Text-extraction fidelity
Extracted text/version
Source-byte hash, parser/OCR configuration, page/span map, quality rule
Source-rendering inspection, mapping checks, controlled rerun
Accepted, corrected-version-required, uncertain, unusable
That extracted statements are true or VLSI-applicable.


Structural conformance
Record or graph
JSON schema, SQL constraints, SHACL shape
Validator/check query
Detailed violations and conformance summary
That meanings match VLSI evidence.


Logical consistency/entailment
Formal graph
OWL/RDF semantics and competency questions
Reasoner and expected-inference tests
Entailments, inconsistencies, unknowns
That axioms are factually or operationally right.


Semantic correctness
Concept/relation/mapping
Versioned domain definitions and project scope
Expert review, counterexample analysis, adjudication
Accepted/rejected/conditional
Retrieval usefulness or user acceptance.


Retrieval performance
Index/release
Versioned query set and relevance judgments
Precision, recall, error analysis
Per-query and aggregate measures
Semantic truth outside the test collection.


Engineering verification
Lifecycle artifact/process
Requirement or claim baseline
Inspection, analysis, demonstration, test, review
Expected vs observed, disposition, evidence
Satisfaction of stakeholder intended use.


Intended-use validation
Release candidate or configuration baseline
Versioned intended uses, users, operational context
Task trials, stakeholder review, usability/relevance study
Fit/not fit/conditional for use
Universal fitness or validity for excluded domains.


Approval decision
Release candidate or governed change
Governance policy, authority, verification/validation package
Independent decision review
Approved, rejected, waived, deferred
Publication or any technical property not evidenced in the package.


Publication
Immutable release candidate
Accepted approval decision, candidate hashes, and publication procedure
Publish/rollback procedure and manifest verification
Succeeded, failed, rolled back
Approval when no accepted decision exists; correctness beyond the approved evidence.




Verification record requirements
Every verification record identifies:

object checked and exact object version;
versioned requirement, claim, reference, or baseline;
procedure/method and procedure version;
tool, tool version, configuration, and relevant environment;
expected result and acceptance rule;
observed result and evidence location;
executor identity and time;
anomalies, uncertainty, and deviations;
disposition: pass, fail, inconclusive, waived, not-run; and
technical reviewer, when required, and follow-up change request.

The same structure applies before implementation. A requirements table, source registry, normalization rule, semantic definition, mapping proposal, schema, test plan, or release note can be verified against its governing baseline.
An approval decision is a separate record made by an authorized role. It identifies the exact target claim, change, or release-candidate baseline; all verification and validation inputs considered; decision and conditions; rationale; authority; time; and any waiver or expiry. The approver may inspect a verification record but does not become the owner of that record. If one person performs both roles, the executor/reviewer act and the approval act still receive different identifiers and timestamps.
A publication event separately identifies the immutable release candidate, accepted approval decision, channel, attempted artifact hashes, actor, time, outcome, and rollback evidence. An accepted approval authorizes but does not perform publication; the successful event creates the release association. A failed publication event leaves the candidate unpublished and preserves the previous successful release as current.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
section: 12. Configuration, versioning, change control, and lifecycle
text:
12. Configuration, versioning, change control, and lifecycle
ISO 10007 identifies configuration-management planning, identification, change control, status accounting, and audit; it applies from concept to disposal.34 ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 covers the full lifecycle through retirement and permits iterative, concurrent, and recursive application of processes.35 Applied here, the lifecycle is:

12.1 Acquisition

Register source authority, identifier, version, access conditions, payload hash, and acquisition activity.
Preserve original payload or state why only a reference/derived record is available.
Record completeness boundaries; an export subset is not “all sessions.”
Classify source, actor, content role, language, and domain scope without altering raw content.



12.2 Normalization and measurement

Baseline normalization rules, tokenizer, protected forms, stop lists, language decisions, grouping rules, and co-occurrence windows.
Treat every rerun as a derivation with output identity.
Retain prior outputs when a rule changes so formula/rule effects can be compared separately from evidence changes.



12.3 Annotation and review

Nominate candidates with evidence and counterexamples.
Review definitions before preferred labels when labels could be homographs.
Record rejected candidates and mappings so failed proposals do not recur without new evidence.
Distinguish review completion from approval for publication.



12.4 Approval, publication, and mapping

Create an immutable release-candidate baseline containing all nodes, including isolated nodes.
Freeze active definitions, labels, relations, mappings, profiles, constraints, intended uses, query sets, and test results.
Record an independent approval decision against that exact baseline and its verification/validation package.
Publish machine-readable and human-readable views only through a publication event that references an accepted decision and the same release hashes.
Record mapping validity by source/target version and intended use.
Preserve the prior successful release until the new publication event succeeds; record failed and rolled-back attempts without rewriting release history.



12.5 Change control, re-verification, and re-validation
A change request states the affected configuration item, rationale, evidence, expected impact, migration treatment, required reviews, and rollback or rejection conditions. Impact analysis traverses dependencies from source and rule through observations, claims, mappings, tests, exports, and releases.
Re-verification checks the changed item against its specified requirement or baseline. It is mandatory when source content/authentication, transformation rules, schemas, inference regimes, concept definitions, predicates, mappings, implementation behavior, or other verifiable configuration properties change.
Re-validation checks fitness for an intended use in its stated users and operational context. It is mandatory, as applicable, when an intended use, user group, operational context, query set, relevance judgment set, retrieval behavior, release limitation, or service interaction changes.
Both impact analyses are required when:

an external standard is revised, withdrawn, or superseded;
a concept definition, preferred label, semantic relation, mapping, or qualifying evidence changes in a way that may affect retrieval or use;
new counterevidence challenges a published assertion or a release-fitness claim; or
a release or migration changes both specified behavior and operational use.

The change-impact record selects reverify, revalidate, both, or neither-with-rationale for every affected claim, intended use, and release. A prior validation record never silently transfers to a changed intended use, and a new verification pass never substitutes for that validation.


12.6 Deprecation and retirement
Deprecation preserves identity, prior definition, validity interval, replacement link, rationale, and retrieval behavior. Retirement occurs only after impact analysis addresses indexed artifacts, mappings, saved queries, dependent claims, intended uses, and reproducibility of historical releases; live dependencies block retirement. Deleted records are tombstoned in the registry, identifiers are never recycled, and a failed release or rollback cannot restore an identifier for a different object.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
section: 13. Failure modes, contamination risks, and mitigations
text:
13. Failure modes, contamination risks, and mitigations









Failure mode
Consequence
Detection
Mitigation




Assistant vocabulary counted as user vocabulary
False personalization and inflated recurrence
Provenance-balance reports; seeded assistant-only token
Actor-specific tables; quoted/source roles; no combined default metric.


Imported paper dominates counts
Corpus reflects document length rather than project usage
Source concentration and per-source contribution
Report raw and source-normalized views separately; do not discard the source.


Mixed-language record admitted wholesale
English index contains Portuguese forms and distorted n-grams
Segment-level language audit
Segment before inclusion; store undecidable status; manual adjudication.


Container-level relevance admits generic segments
Computing, telecom, or geopolicy concepts leak into cid:
Segment-to-applicability coverage query; contamination fixtures
Require an explicit VLSI-applicability record for every cid: segment/concept; otherwise route to ifc:, ext:, pending, or excluded.


Computer Science meaning overwrites VLSI meaning
Wrong definitions, hierarchies, and retrieval
Namespace/source audit; homograph tests
Independent cid:, ext:, ifc: schemes; scoped mappings only.


Co-occurrence represented as a semantic relation
Statistical proximity represented as knowledge
Relation-origin and record-family query
Observation records never enter the reviewed semantic graph; only a separate claim satisfying its evidence profile can appear there.


Domain projection treated as semantic assertion or new evidence
Inflated support and circular graph
Compare graph/view, support-set identities, and derivation links
Keep projection in observation_graph; require a separate admissible claim for reviewed_semantic_graph; count lineage groups.


Mirrors, quotations, or common sources counted independently
Artificial consensus and source dispersion
Evidence-lineage collapse and dependency query
Group common origins; report DF and claim-relative ISF separately; retain unknown independence.


Annotation, review, and approval circularly create domain support
Governed opinion masquerades as VLSI evidence
Claim-profile gate with support-role query
Require qualifying E-DOMAIN or E-PROJECT; governance artifacts cannot satisfy that role.


Score formula creates a claim or release association
Apparent evidence gain without new sources
Diff evidence sets and record IDs against score/config changes
Ranking may nominate review only; it cannot create candidate, claim, decision, or publication records.


Declaration represented as certainty
Unsupported probability claim
Schema rejects probability without calibration metadata
Store assertion method and status; reserve probability for validated models.


Edge-list construction drops isolated nodes
Incomplete concept inventory
Node-count invariant and seeded isolate
Materialize nodes from node registry before edges.


Distinct dates counted as sessions
Inflated dispersion and persistence
Missing authenticated session_id test
Separate date, interaction-group, and session measures.


Summary substitutes for original
Unverifiable quotations and historical labels
Source-authentication check
Preserve payload/hash; label derivative; prohibit “exact” without authenticated original.


Same label treated as equivalence
Cross-scheme semantic collapse
Definition-difference counterexample
Compare intension/extension, versions, and intended use; record conditional mapping.


RDF/OWL domain-range used as input validation
Unexpected inference instead of rejection
Entailment tests with wrong-typed object
Use SHACL/SQL/JSON constraints for closed profiles; document inference regime.


Structural validation called semantic validation
Well-formed but wrong concepts published
Review-evidence coverage query
Separate structural, logical, semantic, retrieval, and intended-use records.


Approval treated as publication
Unpublished or failed artifacts appear current
Approval/publication join and channel audit
Separate decision, immutable release, and publication-event records; retain prior successful release on failure.


Standards revision silently changes baseline
Uncontrolled semantics
Scheduled status review and version diff
Pin editions; open change request; impact analysis; re-verification and/or re-validation according to affected properties.


Graph visualization hides provenance or isolates
Misleading human interpretation
Compare visualization with registry and evidence tables
Treat visualization as a view; require isolate count, edge type, origin, and filters.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
section: 14. Acceptance criteria and future pilot test protocol
text:
14. Acceptance criteria and future pilot test protocol
The future pilot should use a deliberately mixed fixture containing user and assistant messages, quoted passages, uploaded/repository files, code, tool output, mixed English/Portuguese text, two records sharing a date but not a session ID, one isolated concept, one projected domain edge, two identically labeled but differently defined external concepts, and at least one authoritative VLSI standard excerpt or locator. It must also include generic computing text embedded inside a CI-DIGITAL artifact, telecommunications material, Brazil/geopolicy material, construction/BIM material, mirrored and quoted copies of one underlying source, a changed intended use, a superseded standard, a stale claim, a retirement request with live dependencies, an attempted tombstone-ID reuse, a failed publication event, a complete acquisition-to-derived-output provenance chain, and fixtures with unresolved acquisition/procedure/tool/configuration/environment/derivation references.
Numerical thresholds below are pilot engineering acceptance limits, selected to make provenance and transformation defects intolerable while leaving semantic performance to an explicitly versioned test set. They are not claimed as universal quality levels.

14.1 Acquisition and provenance tests








ID
Procedure
Expected result




AP-01
Resolve every admitted segment to its source version and span.
100% resolve; otherwise pilot fails.


AP-02
Recompute hashes for locally retained payloads.
100% equal; unavailable remote/private payloads remain explicitly unauthenticated or partially authenticated.


AP-03
Query occurrences by origin actor/content role.
User, assistant, quotation, file, code, and tool classes are separable with no unclassified admitted segment.


AP-04
Seed a phrase used only by the assistant.
User TF, DF, and significance evidence for the phrase remain zero.


AP-05
Seed a quoted VLSI paragraph in a user message.
Terms count toward quoted-source/file views, not user-authored vocabulary.


AP-06
Seed two records on one date with null session IDs.
distinct_date_count=1; authenticated session frequency remains unavailable.


AP-07
Seed a source, mirror, quotation, summary, and derived measure sharing one underlying passage.
Distinct evidence items remain traceable, but claim-relative ISF=1 under the named rule.


AP-08
Audit every cid-eligible segment and concept.
100% resolve to a versioned segment-level VLSI-applicability record; container-level purpose alone never passes.


AP-09
Traverse every source version and derived artifact through the normalized provenance chain.
Each source resolves its acquisition activity; each derived row resolves one producing derivation run; every run resolves input artifact versions, procedure version, all tool versions, configuration version, environment version, actor/time, logs/evidence, and output identity/hash.


AP-10
Seed records with unresolved acquisition, procedure-version, tool-version, configuration-version, environment-version, input/output-artifact, and derivation-run IDs.
Foreign-key or import validation rejects every dangling reference; no affected artifact can enter analysis, export, approval, or release.





14.2 Deterministic transformation tests








ID
Procedure
Expected result




DT-01
Rerun a clean pipeline with identical inputs/configuration.
Output tables and canonical serialization hashes match exactly.


DT-02
Trace every normalized token to raw spans and applied rules.
100% traceable; no normalization overwrites raw text.


DT-03
Change only a score formula.
Evidence IDs/counts, claim-state events, and ISF do not change.


DT-04
Recompute graph from node and edge registries.
Every in-scope node, including seeded isolate, is present.


DT-05
Project a concept edge to domain level.
Domain edge lists its source edge, remains in observation_graph, never appears as a semantic domain assertion, and reports zero new independent evidence.


DT-06
Run a sparse 2–4-gram fixture below recurrence thresholds.
System reports insufficient recurrence; no candidate phrase is invented.


DT-07
Seed a revised document plus mirrors and derivatives.
DF counts authenticated source versions under its definition; claim-relative ISF collapses common lineage under the named rule and reports unresolved cases as unknown.


DT-08
Extract a two-column PDF with a repeated header and one OCR-degraded VLSI term.
Generic derivation run and extraction specialization jointly retain input/output artifact hashes, procedure/parser/OCR/configuration/environment versions, page-to-span mapping, quality and uncertainty; uncertain high-impact text cannot support a semantic claim without source-rendering inspection.





14.3 Domain and semantic negative tests








ID
Counterexample
Expected result




DS-01
“Verification” in a generic software-process source and in an IC/UVM source.
Two scoped source concepts or definitions remain distinguishable; no silent merge.


DS-02
A construction/BIM “digital twin” document.
Excluded from cid:; may exist in an independent external scheme only if explicitly registered.


DS-03
Co-occurrence of coverage and closure.
Produces an immutable observation that may nominate a separate candidate ID; it creates no skos:related, hierarchy, causality, or semantic claim.


DS-04
A concept assigned to the “verification” domain scheme.
Exports as scheme/facet membership, never automatically as skos:broader.


DS-05
Two external concepts with the same preferred label but different scope.
skos:exactMatch is rejected; mapping is conditional, close, or no-match with definitions retained.


DS-06
A model proposes causes from repeated adjacency.
Candidate record remains separate; no semantic claim or release item exists until qualifying evidence and reviewer acceptance support them.


DS-07
A VLSI concept with no current edge.
Concept remains in the published node inventory if independently accepted.


DS-08
A CI-DIGITAL verification plan contains a generic database transaction, OAuth, or software-build passage with no explicit IC applicability.
Segment is not admitted to cid: because of its container; it is routed to ifc:, an applicable ext: scheme, pending, or excluded.


DS-09
A telecommunications architecture passage is embedded inside a CI-DIGITAL/VLSI project package and uses terms also found in IC design.
Passage and meanings remain outside cid: unless exact segment-level VLSI applicability is separately evidenced; container and label overlap do not admit it.


DS-10
A Brazil policy/geography passage is embedded inside the same CI-DIGITAL/VLSI container as semiconductor material.
Geography and policy concepts remain excluded from cid: or independently registered in ext:; container proximity creates no domain relation.


DS-11
A projected concept-to-domain edge is submitted for semantic publication.
Submission fails because a projection is analytical evidence only; a separate semantic claim with its own predicate and admissible support is required.


DS-12
An annotation is reviewed and approved without qualifying VLSI evidence or a versioned CI-DIGITAL project requirement.
Publication gate fails even when E-ANNOTATION, E-REVIEW, and E-DECISION are present.





14.4 Structural and logical tests

All identifiers are unique, immutable, and resolve in the release.
Required fields satisfy relational/JSON constraints; RDF exports satisfy the versioned SHACL profile when one is adopted.
Every published concept has at least one definition or scope note, a language-tagged preferred label for the release language, scheme membership, provenance, a satisfied claim-type evidence profile, review, an independent approval decision, and a successful publication event.
Every semantic edge uses a registered predicate with direction, scope, domain/range policy, evidence, review, and status.
Every mapping links identified concept versions from different schemes and includes intended use.
Expected-inference tests pass; prohibited-inference tests do not appear under the declared entailment regime.
Structural conformance, reasoner outcome, semantic review, retrieval evaluation, approval decision, and publication event remain separate records.



14.5 Retrieval and intended-use validation
Create a versioned query set representing at least these CI-DIGITAL tasks:

find all sources supporting a SystemVerilog/UVM verification concept;
distinguish functional coverage, code coverage, assertion coverage, and test coverage;
retrieve verification artifacts by lifecycle role: requirement, plan, procedure, configuration, result, waiver, defect;
locate DFT/test-access concepts without conflating verification methodology;
trace a published relation to exact evidence and counterevidence;
retrieve historical terms after deprecation without assigning them to new content; and
show a concept’s observed evolution without using assistant-originated language as user evidence.

Two VLSI/EDA reviewers should independently judge relevance for a stratified sample; disagreements are adjudicated and retained. The pilot reports per-query precision and recall, macro and micro summaries, unanswerable queries, provenance errors, semantic false positives, and reviewer disagreement. Initial release thresholds should be set only after a baseline run exposes task difficulty. The non-negotiable gate is zero known provenance-class or domain-boundary violations in the seeded negative tests.


14.6 Lifecycle and release negative tests








ID
Counterexample
Expected result




LC-01
A published claim still references a replaced source, rule, or evidence baseline without completed impact disposition.
A separate stale-impact record blocks that claim version from a new release/use until required re-verification and/or re-validation completes; historical releases remain unchanged.


LC-02
An intended use or query/relevance set changes while prior validation remains passing.
Prior validation remains historical; the changed use is unvalidated until a new or explicitly justified re-validation record completes.


LC-03
A cited standard is superseded or withdrawn.
Version remains preserved; change request and dependency impact open; affected claims are not silently rebound and receive required re-verification and/or re-validation.


LC-04
Retirement is requested for a concept with live claims, mappings, indexed assignments, saved queries, or intended uses.
Retirement is blocked until dependencies are migrated, retired, or explicitly dispositioned by an authorized decision.


LC-05
A deleted/tombstoned identifier is assigned to a new term, concept, claim, evidence item, or release.
Referential/uniqueness constraint rejects reuse; historical identity remains resolvable.


LC-06
Publication fails after approval or a new release is rolled back.
Failure/rollback event is recorded; no current-release association is created, the prior successful release remains current, and approval is not rewritten as publication.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
section: 15. Minimum viable implementation stages and stopping gates
text:
15. Minimum viable implementation stages and stopping gates
No corpus pipeline is implemented in this study. The recommended staged implementation is:

Stage 0 — Governance and identifiers
Deliver source/classification policies, segment-level VLSI-applicability rules, identifier rules, evidence/claim statuses and admissibility profiles, intended-use records, predicate registry, executor/reviewer/approver/publisher role separation, and configuration-item inventory covering procedures, tools, configurations, environments, acquisition activities, and derivation runs.
Stop gate: do not ingest at scale until user/assistant/quotation/file/code/tool provenance classes and the cid:/ext:/ifc: boundary are approved.


Stage 1 — Immutable corpus registry
Implement source/version/segment and artifact-version registries; acquisition activities; versioned procedure, tool, configuration, and execution-environment registries; generic derivation runs with normalized input/tool/output links; extraction specializations and page/span maps; domain-applicability/admission decisions; evidence lineage; payload hashes; language/scope decisions; and temporal uncertainty.
Stop gate: do not compute user vocabulary until AP-01 through AP-10 and DT-08 pass.


Stage 2 — Deterministic lexical oracle
Implement reversible normalization, protected VLSI forms, token/lemma/n-gram occurrences, TF/DF/ISF/SF/IGF, actor-specific measures, temporal windows, and generic derivation-run manifests for every produced artifact.
Stop gate: do not issue recurrence/trend claims until deterministic tests pass and corpus-adequacy rules are declared.


Stage 3 — Observation graph and candidates
Implement observation_graph with all-node materialization, co-occurrence and distribution observations, projected analytical edges, candidate-term records, and candidate-relation packages. Preserve raw signal vectors and evidence lineage; do not assign a confidence probability.
Stop gate: do not export observational edges as semantic predicates.


Stage 4 — Reviewed concept index
Add definitions, labels, domain/facet assignments, external authority locators, claim-type evidence-profile enforcement, counterexamples, review/adjudication, and immutable nomination/claim/review links.
Stop gate: no concept claim enters a release candidate without accepted scope, qualifying evidence, review, and intended use. Approval remains a separate decision and does not publish it; publication requires the later successful event in Stage 6.


Stage 5 — Typed semantic graph and mappings
Introduce a separate reviewed_semantic_graph, predicate registry, semantic edges, external scheme/version registry, mapping conditions, impact analysis, and source-to-claim traceability.
Stop gate: no mapping or projected relation may manufacture independent evidence; negative semantic tests must pass.


Stage 6 — Representation profiles and service validation
Add stable exports, optional RDF/SKOS, SHACL profiles, retrieval evaluation, release assurance arguments, release_governance_view, independent approvals, publication events, rollback, and lifecycle automation. OWL is introduced only for approved competency questions requiring formal inference.
Publication gate: no event succeeds unless the candidate hashes match the approved baseline, required verification and validation records remain current, the accepted decision authorizes that exact candidate, and a rollback target/procedure is recorded.
Stop gate: do not call the artifact an ontology until the ontology threshold in Section 8.5 and logical test suite are satisfied.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
text:
16. Promotion criteria
Here “promotion” is shorthand for creating a new immutable record and typed link after a gate passes; it never mutates an observation, candidate, claim version, decision, or event into another record type.







New immutable record or link
Required evidence and decision




Source segment yields observation
Authenticated or bounded source identity; deterministic procedure/configuration; reversible locator; reproducible result; new observation ID.


Observation nominates candidate term/concept
Named nomination rule; supporting occurrences; provenance distribution; corpus-adequacy result; new candidate ID; no semantic claim implied.


Observation nominates candidate relation
Exact window/signal definitions; root evidence set; direction proposal, if any; model/rule origin; projected-evidence flag; new candidate ID.


Candidate supports_creation_of proposed claim version
Scoped definition/predicate; qualifying E-DOMAIN or E-PROJECT support under the claim-type profile; counterevidence; intended use; mapping/domain analysis; new claim ID/version.


Review record accepts or rejects claim version
Independent review, disagreements/adjudication, condition of applicability, known limitations, immutable disposition record.


Release item includes accepted claim version
Structural and semantic checks; required logical/retrieval checks for use; current validation for intended uses; change-impact record; immutable release-candidate hash.


Approval decision authorizes_publication_of release candidate
Exact candidate baseline; verification/validation inputs; independent authority, rationale, conditions, and decision ID.


Publication event associates claim versions with release
Accepted approval decision; exact release hashes; successful outcome; prior-current-release handling; new event ID.


Deprecation record limits_new_use_of published item
Change request; replacement/no-replacement decision; validity interval; migration and historical retrieval treatment.


Retirement decision retires deprecated item
Dependency and indexed-content impact complete; historical reproducibility retained; authorized decision and tombstone.



No record or link above is created automatically because a count exceeds a threshold. Thresholds may prioritize review; they cannot replace an admissible record-creation procedure.

Preferred initial form

SQLite

SQLite + JSON manifest

SQLite

SQLite

SQLite + JSON
impact ID, change/source/standard trigger FK, dependency closure, affected claim/use/release FKs, stale-impact findings, reverify/revalidate/both/neither-with-rationale selections, completion state.

SQLite

SQLite

Markdown + structured JSON

TSV exports should be normalized and joinable by stable IDs, not treated as the canonical store. JSON should use explicit arrays and nulls rather than comma-packed fields. SQLite should enforce identity, the foreign keys shown above, evidence-profile gates, nonreusable tombstones, valid immutable-event sequences, and uniqueness. Every source version resolves an acquisition_activity_id; every derived concrete row resolves both an artifact_version_id and its producing derivation_run_id; and every run resolves its procedure, tools, configuration, environment, inputs, outputs, actor/time, and log/evidence records. These invariants are checked before export and release, including for imported Parquet/JSON data. The named provenance/evidence, observation, reviewed-semantic, and release/governance graph/views are constructed from these registries; no format or view alone supplies provenance, semantics, approval, or publication.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
text:
18. CI-DIGITAL-specific translation

18.1 Domain structure
The index should begin with multiple facets rather than one forced tree:







Facet
Illustrative values




Lifecycle/activity
requirements, architecture, RTL design, synthesis, physical implementation, verification planning, simulation, formal verification, DFT insertion, ATPG, manufacturing test, post-silicon test, debug.


Physical-design/signoff activity
floorplanning, power planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, parasitic extraction, static timing analysis, signal-integrity analysis, power-integrity/EM-IR analysis, DRC, LVS, ERC, timing/power/physical signoff.


Artifact
specification, HDL module, assertion, testbench, stimulus model, coverage model, netlist, floorplan, timing/power constraint, routed layout, parasitic extraction, timing/power/DRC/LVS result, fault model, test pattern, result database, waiver, defect report.


Verification method
inspection, lint/static analysis, simulation, assertion-based verification, formal proof/model checking, equivalence checking, emulation, FPGA prototyping, coverage analysis.


Test method
scan, boundary scan, embedded-core test, IJTAG/instrument access, memory BIST, logic BIST, ATPG, wafer/final test, 3D stack access.


Design concern
functionality, timing, power, area, signal integrity, power integrity, clock/reset domain crossing, analog/mixed signal, reliability, security, manufacturability, testability.


Evidence role
requirement, assumption, procedure, configuration, expected result, observed result, coverage evidence, proof artifact, anomaly, disposition.



Facet membership permits a coverage_model to participate in functional verification, a UVM testbench, and a lifecycle stage without claiming three competing parents. Hierarchies may later be added inside a facet when an authoritative generic, instance, or part-whole relation is established.


18.2 Domain predicate examples
Candidate domain predicates should be narrower than generic related_to:

specifies_requirement_for
implements_design_intent_of
verified_against
validated_for_use_in
exercises
observes
measures_coverage_of
generates_stimulus_for
detects_faults_represented_by
provides_test_access_to
configured_by
produces_result
waives_with_rationale
supersedes

Each needs a definition and counterexample. For instance, a coverage metric may measure exercised model items without proving requirement satisfaction; a test may detect faults represented by a model without proving absence of all physical defects; and a passing simulation may provide evidence for a requirement without validating silicon in its intended environment.
Predicates such as verified_against and validated_for_use_in are conceptual relations only. Asserting either one never creates a verification or validation record, never supplies a procedure or observed result, and never assigns a pass/fail/fit disposition. Those process records must be independently instantiated under Section 11 and linked as evidence where admissible.


18.3 Example evidence chain
IEEE 1800-2023 / project verification plan / RTL source version
        -> authenticated source segments
        -> observed terms: assertion, cover property, functional coverage
        -> candidate concept: assertion-based verification
        -> reviewed definition and scoped labels
        -> semantic assertions linking artifact, method, and evidence roles
        -> retrieval and traceability tests
        -> approved concept-graph release
The standard anchors language meaning; the project plan anchors intended use; source files and results anchor project evidence. None substitutes for the others.


18.4 Handling domain boundaries in practice

Formal methods enters cid: only through a VLSI use such as property checking, equivalence, or SAT-based verification; broader AI/formal-method classifications remain ifc: or ext:.
Graph visualization remains a presentation concern. A layout cluster must not become a domain or semantic relation because it looks coherent.
Software artifacts inside verification environments can be represented as artifacts without importing a generic software taxonomy as the parent of IC verification.
Telecommunications material remains outside cid: unless an exact segment is separately evidenced as applicable to an IC artifact, method, or requirement; shared words such as “network,” “channel,” or “verification” do not establish that applicability.
Brazil or other geographic/policy context is metadata or an independent external scheme when needed. Archive co-location and project sponsorship do not turn geography, industrial policy, or regulation into VLSI concepts.
AI/ML for EDA claims retain model, dataset, toolchain, design/node, uncertainty, and evaluation context. The repository’s NSF workshop report emphasizes data availability, generalization, scalability, reliability, and robust infrastructure, which should become evidence obligations rather than vocabulary alone.36
Industry ontologies such as Si2’s 2026 AI-for-EDA release are mapped as external schemes. Their agentic-workflow purpose and release version remain explicit; only reviewed VLSI meanings are admitted to cid:.37



18.5 Initial CI-DIGITAL release objective
The first useful release is not “all semiconductor knowledge.” It is a small, auditable index capable of answering:

Which English terms and phrases recur in authenticated CI-DIGITAL sources, by provenance class and time?
Which reviewed concepts do those terms designate in VLSI/IC design, verification, or test?
Which artifact, activity, concern, method, lifecycle, and evidence facets apply?
Which relations are observations, which are reviewed semantic assertions, and which are external mappings?
What exact evidence and lineage, counterevidence, review, verification, validation, approval decision, and publication event supports each published item?
What changed between releases, what depended on the change, and what was re-verified and/or re-validated?

If the implementation answers these questions without provenance leakage or semantic inflation, it has achieved a defensible concept index and typed concept graph. Formal ontology work can then be justified by concrete competency questions rather than by the appeal of a more formal label.

title: Evidence-First Methodology for a Governed CI-DIGITAL Concept Index and Typed Concept Graph
text:
19. Recommended engineering decision
Adopt this methodology as the baseline for a future pilot, with four binding controls:

Evidence identity before semantics: no published item without exact source/derivation traceability.
VLSI domain independence: no cross-domain meaning without an explicit interface scheme and scoped mapping.
Typed epistemic states: observation, candidate, reviewed assertion, verification, validation, approval, and publication are separate records.
Lifecycle assurance: every material change triggers impact analysis, re-verification and/or re-validation according to the affected property, an independent release decision, and a separately recorded publication outcome.

The immediate next deliverable should be Stage 0: a compact governance specification and schema prototype derived from Sections 5, 6, 10, 16, and 17. Corpus ingestion should wait until those controls can be tested against the negative fixture.
