title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
section: One word should name one role
text:
One word should name one role
Several tools can report a red underline, but they do not necessarily perform the same operation.









Term
Primary role
Typical result
Usually changes source?




Syntax highlighter
Classifies tokens for display
Colors and text scopes
No


Language server or language service
Maintains a semantic model for an editor
Completion, hover, navigation, symbols, references, diagnostics, and sometimes formatting
Usually no; code actions and formatting may propose or apply edits


Linter
Checks source against static rules
Diagnostics with locations and explanations
No by default; some linters offer explicit fixes


Formatter
Rewrites layout according to a style
Indentation, spacing, line wrapping, and brace placement where supported
Yes when its result is accepted or written


Compiler
Translates source and checks the language while doing so
Object code, an executable, and compiler diagnostics
It normally creates build artifacts, not source edits


Interpreter
Evaluates source directly
Program behavior, output, and runtime errors
It can cause any side effects permitted by the program


Solver
Searches for a model, proof result, or satisfying assignment
sat, unsat, unknown, a model, or solver diagnostics
No source edit by default



These are roles, not mutually exclusive product categories. One implementation may supply several roles. Tcl LSP, for example, provides language-server features, diagnostics, and formatting. A compiler can also supply diagnostics that an editor presents like lint results. LSP is a communication protocol; not every editor language service uses it.
crumbs: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries

title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
text:
Where a capability can live
VS Code presents one interface over several distinct execution layers:





flowchart LR
    S[Source file] --> V[VS Code Flatpak]
    V --> B[Built-in language feature]
    V --> E[Extension with bundled engine]
    V --> C[Extension acting as a client]
    C --> X[Executable visible inside Flatpak]
    C -. explicit host bridge .-> H[Executable on Fedora host]
    S --> D[Direct command-line caller]
    D --> H







Built into VS Code. The editor ships and updates the implementation.
Bundled by a user extension. The extension contains its own server, parser, formatter, or solver.
Supplied externally. The extension is only a client or wrapper and expects a separate executable.
Installed on the Fedora host. A terminal, script, or local agent can call the executable without VS Code.

The current VS Code installation is a Flatpak. Its extension host does not inherit the Fedora host’s normal executable path. An executable can therefore be present and directly callable on Fedora while still being invisible to an extension. The integrated terminal’s host-shell configuration does not change the extension host. External-tool extensions need an explicit path, wrapper, or flatpak-spawn --host bridge.
This creates four useful verification states:

Declared: a setting or extension manifest advertises the capability.
Present: the required component exists in its execution environment.
Reachable: the intended caller can start it.
Exercised: it has processed a representative file or command successfully.

An extension entry in Settings proves only the first or second state. It does not, by itself, prove that a backend is reachable or working.

Available bridge patterns
Flatpak is one present client boundary, not the target architecture. The broader objective is to make verified local tools available to editors, agents, command-line workflows, and other authorized clients. There is no single universal bridge, but four patterns are technically sound:








Pattern
When it fits
Tradeoff




Install the backend inside Flatpak
The package or a compatible Flatpak SDK extension exists
Simple for the editor, but it creates a second installation that can drift from the Fedora host


Use a flatpak-spawn --host wrapper
The extension accepts a configurable executable or command
Reuses the authoritative host installation; the wrapper and Flatpak permissions must be explicit


Connect to a server through TCP or a Unix socket
Both the language server and editor client support a network address
Clean process separation, but LSP support over a socket is implementation-specific and socket visibility must cross the sandbox


Install the upstream standalone tool in both environments
Exact isolation is desirable and duplicate management is acceptable
Predictable within each environment, but versions must be checked independently



The reverse direction is also possible when an extension bundles a tool that is published separately: install the upstream command on Fedora and use that public interface from terminals and automation. Depending on a private binary inside an extension is fragile because its path, permissions, and version belong to the extension’s packaging rather than to the host toolchain.
For this workstation, an authoritative editor-independent interface should be the default. An editor-specific wrapper can consume that interface when needed. A bundled engine remains appropriate when it is self-contained and already works, as with the current Tcl, Prolog, and SMT extensions.

title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
text:
Candidate editor-independent service boundary
The common service should not automate VS Code. It should expose the public interfaces of the underlying tools, allowing VS Code, local agents, scripts, and other clients to become peers.








Backend
Verified native interface
Smallest safe adapter




Tcl toolchain
CLI accepts files, directories, or inline source; diagnostics can be JSON; rewritten source goes to a selected file or standard output
Supervised one-shot process for validate, lint, format, graphs, and other batch operations


Tcl MCP
MCP protocol over standard input/output
Direct MCP connection for agent clients


Tcl language server
LSP JSON-RPC over standard input/output
Persistent per-workspace process only when completion, navigation, or live diagnostics are needed


SWI-Prolog
CLI accepts source files and explicit goals; the host also supplies libswipl
One-shot CLI for bounded queries; a persistent Prolog service only for an explicitly stateful use case


Z3
CLI accepts SMT-LIB files or standard input and returns solver results on standard output
One-shot solver process with time and memory limits


GCC, G++, GNU Fortran, and TypeScript compiler
CLI accepts project or source inputs and reports through exit status and output streams
Isolated compile/check job with an explicit artifact directory


gofmt, AStyle, HTML Tidy, and xmllint
File mode and/or standard input to standard output
Transform request that returns proposed text or a diff instead of overwriting the caller’s file


Extension-private engines
Internal extension process or protocol
Do not use as the shared boundary unless the same engine publishes a stable standalone interface



MCP is a good client-facing protocol for agent tools. A small HTTP, Unix-socket, or ordinary command interface can serve non-MCP clients. The backend adapter does not need to use the same protocol: it can translate one bounded request into a CLI process, an LSP session, or a solver invocation.
A minimal request needs:

Operation: validate, lint, format, compile-check, interpret, or solve.
Language and dialect.
Source text or an explicitly bounded set of files.
Tool-specific options and resource limits.
Whether generated artifacts are permitted.

A useful response needs:

Exact tool identity and version.
Exit status and elapsed time.
Structured diagnostics when available.
Preserved standard output and standard error.
Proposed rewritten source or a diff, never an unannounced write.
Explicit artifact paths when compilation is authorized.

Rootless Podman is feasible as a packaging and isolation layer, especially when a backend is large, has conflicting dependencies, or should be reproducible for other users. Batch tools should normally start on demand and exit. Language servers may remain alive per workspace because their value comes from maintaining an index. In either case, use read-only source mounts by default, a scratch output directory, no network unless required, and CPU, memory, process, and time limits.
This separation also prevents a workspace-indexing language server from being treated like a trivial formatter. Both consume source, but the server may retain state and search an entire tree, while a formatter can usually be a stateless transformation of one document.

Microservice-like aggregation
The useful pattern is a stable front door with isolated tool workers, rather than one process that pretends every capability has the same semantics.





flowchart LR
    A[Agent or MCP client] --> G[Tool broker]
    C[Command-line client] --> G
    E[Editor client] --> G
    R[Remote authorized client] --> G
    G --> V[Validate request and select profile]
    V --> O[On-demand batch worker]
    V --> P[Persistent workspace worker]
    O --> N[Evidence envelope]
    P --> N
    N --> G







On-demand workers fit lint, format, compile-check, interpretation, and solver jobs that can be reproduced from explicit inputs.
Persistent workspace workers fit LSP servers and indexers whose value depends on retained project state.
Profiles bind a language or domain to a tool version, dialect, rules, limits, and permitted operations without merging those domains.
The evidence envelope gives every response common provenance fields while retaining the backend’s native output.

Containers make each worker reproducible, replaceable, resource-bounded, and deployable on another local or remote host. They do not require every worker to become a permanently running network service. Starting stateless workers on demand avoids idle resource use and limits the number of background indexers.
Fast responses come from keeping only the state that earns its cost: a cached capability registry, warm images, persistent indices for active workspaces, and event-driven invalidation when source or configuration changes. The broker may aggregate results, but it should not erase which tool, profile, version, and input produced each result.
This is intentionally microservice-like, not a conclusion that a large distributed microservice platform is already required. Container boundaries and common contracts provide most of the portability and isolation benefits. Network discovery, retries, distributed tracing, replicated state, and orchestration should be added only when a real remote or multi-host use case requires them.
Podman 5.8.4 is present on this workstation, so the container boundary is locally feasible. The architecture above is a recorded candidate, not an implemented service: no image, broker, socket, daemon, or remote endpoint was created during this inventory.

title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
section: Tcl formatting and the Whitesmiths requirement
text:
Tcl formatting and the Whitesmiths requirement
The project’s desired visual signature is specifically the placement and alignment of block braces in Whitesmiths style. It is not merely a tab choice or an indentation width.
The current Tcl formatter cannot produce that signature. Its only exposed brace style is k_and_r. It can normalize indentation and whitespace, but it leaves opening block braces at the end of their command line. Running it therefore does not satisfy the requirement even when the resulting body indentation changes.
Tcl also makes this more than a cosmetic substitution. An unescaped newline terminates a command, so blindly moving an opening brace to a line of its own can change or break the program. The official Tcl style guide states that an opening brace cannot appear alone and should remain at the end of the preceding line. The installed formatter’s formatting specification exposes only K&R brace placement.
A robust Whitesmiths feature for Tcl would therefore need all of the following:

Tcl-aware parsing rather than a textual brace-moving rule.
A semantics-preserving continuation strategy wherever a block brace moves.
Coverage for Tcl 9 and each relevant embedded EDA dialect.
Idempotence: formatting the result again must produce no further change.
Execution or parser comparisons on representative scripts before adoption.

That feature is feasible, but it is not present today. Format-on-save remains disabled so the existing K&R-only formatter cannot silently erase the intended visual marker.
crumbs: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries

title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
section: Tool routing for local, observable work
text:
Tool routing for local, observable work
Deterministic local tools should answer mechanically checkable questions before an AI system interprets the result.








Question
First tool
AI contribution after the tool




Is this token sequence valid Tcl?
Tcl parser/interpreter or Tcl diagnostics
Explain the error in project context and propose a bounded correction


Does the source violate static rules?
Linter or language-server diagnostics
Correlate findings, distinguish signal from noise, and prioritize


Does layout match the selected style?
Formatter plus a source diff
Explain exceptional cases and verify that no unintended semantic edit occurred


Does C, C++, Fortran, Go, or TypeScript type-check or compile?
Corresponding compiler/toolchain
Interpret diagnostics and relate them to design intent


Is an SMT constraint satisfiable?
Z3
Explain the model, assumptions, and limits of the result


What changed?
Version-control diff and preserved command output
Relate the observable delta to the stated requirement



This division reduces speculative work. A compiler or solver supplies reproducible evidence; AI is then used for synthesis, explanation, cross-domain reasoning, and carefully bounded changes. When provenance matters, retain the invoked command, tool version, input identity, raw result, and resulting diff rather than only a prose retelling.
The action footprint still matters:

Highlighting, navigation, and ordinary linting are read-only observations.
Formatting becomes a source mutation when its result is accepted.
Compilation normally creates artifacts even when it does not edit source.
Interpretation executes a program and can trigger its permitted side effects.
Solver execution is normally read-only with respect to the source, but its result depends on the exact assertions and solver version.

title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
text:
Evidence behind this inventory
The snapshot was assembled from observable sources rather than from extension names alone:

Host command resolution and version output.
Fedora package records for the host runtimes and compilers.
The VS Code Flatpak’s own shell view of executable availability.
VS Code’s extension registry and disabled-extension state.
Installed extension manifests, bundled files, and declared providers.
Current VS Code user settings.
Current Tcl LSP initialization logs.

The relevant VS Code state lives under the user Flatpak data and configuration directories. Built-in language features live under the active system Flatpak installation. Extension-private binaries are evidence of a bundled capability, not stable system interfaces.
Installed versions describe this workstation only. Before recommending a new dependency or treating one as a durable project choice, also verify its upstream release date, recent maintenance, supported language versions, and unresolved issues. That maintenance check was outside this local inventory and is therefore not implied here.

text:
Rechecking the snapshot
The host inventory can be refreshed without VS Code:
command -v swipl z3 tclsh go gofmt gcc g++ gfortran tsc astyle tidy xmllint
swipl --version
z3 --version
printf 'puts [info patchlevel]\n' | tclsh
go version
gcc --version | head -n 1
gfortran --version | head -n 1
tsc --version
The Flatpak view must be checked separately. This example demonstrates the version boundary rather than changing it:
flatpak run --command=sh com.visualstudio.code -lc \
    'command -v gfortran; gfortran --version | head -n 1'
The final check belongs at the point of use: open or process a representative file, observe which implementation responds, retain its output, and avoid inferring an operational capability from a settings page alone.

title: Local language tooling: capabilities and boundaries
text:
Subsequent implemented container boundary
After the inventory and architectural candidate were recorded, a separate authorized step implemented the first container boundary at language-toolbox/. This changes the earlier statement about no image having been created; it does not promote the proposed broker, socket service, or remote endpoint into implemented components.
The image packages the editor-independent Tcl, Prolog, Z3, C, C++, Fortran, Go, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, XML, and C-like formatting tools behind one foreground entry point. It uses a digest-pinned Fedora base, exact direct RPM versions, checked Tcl release artifacts, and a version-pinned Go language server. The runtime lock records those inputs.
Verification established four distinct levels rather than collapsing them:

The image built from the recorded sources and package versions.
Every installed tool family processed a representative input under a read-only, network-disabled, capability-dropped container invocation.
Tcl LSP and gopls each completed a real LSP initialization exchange.
Tcl MCP and gopls mcp each completed a real MCP initialization exchange.

The resulting image is below 1 GB unpacked. That size is dominated by the actual compiler toolchains and three independent Tcl analysis executables, not by an editor or graphical environment. The exact image identity, size, checks, and remaining boundaries are retained in the build record.

Go is the selected implementation language for a later common broker or protocol adapter if that next layer is authorized. This is a forward implementation decision, not evidence that the broker already exists.

title: Requirements
text:
Functional Requirements







ID
Requirement




FR-001
Register every canonical entity under one typed stable identifier that is never reused.


FR-002
Preserve immutable source routing/revision, source-version, acquisition, explicit artifact identity-state, extracted-text, and exact covering-span records.


FR-003
Resolve every source version to matching acquisition authentication/completeness plus a versioned procedure, applicable configuration/tools or omission rationale, environment, actor, time, and artifact.


FR-004
Resolve every derived concrete row to one producing derivation run, output artifact/hash, procedure, tools or omission rationale, configuration, environment, actor, times, and inputs whose exact observed identity state/hash/unavailable rationale equals the registered artifact tuple.


FR-005
Support identity extraction for UTF-8 plain text/Markdown and provenance-complete import of externally extracted text; never execute PDF/OCR/parser software internally.


FR-006
Segment with explicit actor, origin class, content role, language decision, scope decision, reversible offsets, and time/session uncertainty.


FR-007
Activate claim-level cid governance when the explicit scope, predicate namespace, or either endpoint is cid; require exact active cid scope, non-empty locator, typed facets, basis-conditioned support, entity-level applicability, and accepted admission. Permit scope none only for an explicitly non-semantic profile.


FR-008
Normalize deterministically without overwriting raw text and retain an ordered output-character to source-character map.


FR-009
Materialize sentence, token, lemma, and contiguous n-gram occurrences with ordered token membership.


FR-010
Compute TF, DF, SF, IGF, UF, AF, first-seen, and last-seen without treating frequency as importance or significance.


FR-011
Store one exact coherent evidence/source/segment membership chain for every aggregate, observation edge, and similarity signal; a hash alone is insufficient.


FR-012
Compute claim-relative ISF by the profile’s named lineage rule over exact available supporting role/class evidence; exclude/report unknown independence and never trust an assessment-wide scalar as the gate.


FR-013
Materialize all graph nodes before edges and retain isolates.


FR-014
Keep co-occurrence, precedence, independent source-distribution similarity-signal records, and domain projection in observation_graph.


FR-015
Make projections retain source-edge root membership/hash and add zero independent evidence.


FR-016
Create separate candidate records only by an explicit nomination command; no threshold may auto-create a candidate.


FR-017
Create separate term, concept, claim, review, V&V, decision, release, and publication records; no record changes family.


FR-018
Bind every claim to the exact recomputed seal of a versioned profile with at least one positive requirement, and bind concept-definition claims to exact concept version/text/scope/applicability.


FR-019
Express profile alternatives as requirement groups; every group must pass at least one typed evidence alternative.


FR-020
Permit qualifying E-DOMAIN only through an authenticated source/version plus a typed normative or authoritative external domain warrant; informative warrants never satisfy support, counts, ISF, review, or release gates.


FR-021
Permit qualifying E-PROJECT only through an approved versioned CI-DIGITAL requirement.


FR-022
Ensure every claim-evidence independence link names an assessment for the same claim and included evidence item.


FR-023
Enforce profile minimum counts and minimum ISF before reviewed acceptance, release approval, and publication.


FR-024
Keep internal cid and ifc schemes versioned; require ext concepts to name an external scheme version.


FR-025
Require a scoped mapping whose scheme IDs equal the concepts’ actual distinct owning scheme versions; shared labels never imply equivalence.


FR-026
Produce exactly four mandatory named graph/views without collapsing epistemic states.


FR-027
Keep verification, intended-use validation, retrieval, assurance, approval, and publication independent; validation/retrieval count as current only when bound to the current approved use, matching user group/context, and current sealed query/relevance baseline.


FR-028
Freeze each release item’s exact canonical record/version/hash in a non-recursive immutable content artifact, include every live graph node, and separately freeze the complete release-relative definition/label/facet/assertion/predicate/mapping/profile/use/query/V&V/retrieval/assurance closure in a versioned post-V&V approval package. Later packages for unchanged release content must explicitly supersede the current package head.


FR-029
Permit successful publication only for the exact approved current-head approval-package hash, complete current gates/inputs, traversed role separation, satisfied assurance, and exactly one transition mode: first-channel bootstrap with evidence and no rollback fields, or later advance naming the immediate effective same-channel release plus rollback procedure/evidence.


FR-030
Derive current release per channel only from ordered successful bootstrap/advance and rollback events; rollback must replace the immediate current release with a previously successful target whose publication-bound package remains its valid current head, while failed attempts never change state and historical events are not retroactively rejudged by later package supersession.


FR-031
Record changes, dependency closure, stale claim events, re-verification/re-validation obligations, deprecation, retirement, and tombstones append-only.


FR-032
Block retirement while live claims, mappings, or currently published release dependencies remain.


FR-033
Export deterministic canonical JSON and normalized TSV with stable ordering and SHA-256 hashes.


FR-034
Refuse release export unless the release is currently published and its exact publication-bound approval package is also the valid current package head whose frozen snapshots, content artifact, and dependent validators pass.

ID
Requirement

NFR-003

NFR-004

Preserve immutable release content, approval packages, baseline snapshots, old versions, and successful historical releases after failures, supersession, deprecation, or retirement.

title: Data Model
text:
Identity Model

A stable ID identifies one immutable version record, not a mutable logical object.
Logical continuity uses *_key + version, supersedes_*, validity intervals, or state-event links.
Every typed insert requires the same ID/type to be preregistered and live; Python registers it in the same transaction.
stable_identifiers cannot be deleted. Its only permitted update is the tombstone time caused by a matching tombstone trigger.
A tombstoned ID remains resolvable and cannot be registered under any type again.

title: Data Model
text:
Acquisition and Derivation Invariants

An acquisition artifact has exactly producer_kind='acquisition', one acquisition activity, and no derivation run.
A derived artifact has exactly producer_kind='derivation', one derivation run, and no acquisition activity.
Artifact identity is explicitly available with a hash or unavailable with a non-empty rationale; null never silently means either state.
Every selected configuration is explicitly applicable to the procedure and every linked tool used by its acquisition, derivation, verification, or validation act.
Every successful derivation has input and output links plus tool versions or an explicit no-tool rationale. Each input records the exact observed identity state/hash/unavailable rationale; no field is inferred from the current artifact row.
Every concrete derived row’s artifact_version_id and derivation_run_id match both artifact_versions and derivation_run_outputs; the output hash equals the artifact identity hash, including the explicit unavailable state.
Every source version’s artifact producer matches its acquisition_activity_id.
Source authentication/completeness and payload hash match that acquisition activity and artifact identity; routing changes form an immutable reviewed supersession chain.
Extraction binds exactly extraction_run -> derivation input/output -> extracted_text -> span -> segment; each segment’s required span covers its complete half-open range. The UTF-8 byte hash is a typed artifact_content_identity bound to output artifact/run/content role and is not equated to the extraction bundle’s identity hash.
Every release item’s stored canonical JSON and hash recompute from the exact typed record. The release manifest is the identity/output hash of a non-recursive content artifact containing release metadata and item snapshots.

title: Data Model
text:
Evidence and Warrant Invariants

E-SOURCE binds an authenticated source version or a segment from it.
E-DERIVED binds the exact artifact producer run and registered output.
E-DOMAIN requires domain_warrant_id; the warrant binds an external scheme version, authenticated source version, exact locator, scope, normative/authoritative status, and optional source segment. Informative warrants remain records but never qualify.
E-PROJECT requires project_requirement_id; the target requirement version must be approved.
Other evidence classes cannot populate those warrant fields.
Aggregate, edge, and similarity hashes are recomputable from normalized memberships; any supplied evidence item, source version, and segment must be the exact same provenance chain.
A projected edge copies the complete source membership, keeps the same membership hash, records its source edge, and has independent evidence delta zero.

title: Data Model
Data Model
text:
Scheme Model

concept_schemes and versions own internal cid and ifc namespaces.
external_schemes and versions own ext concepts.
A cid/ifc concept names exactly one matching internal scheme version and no external scheme.
An ext concept names exactly one external scheme version and no internal scheme.
A mapping’s source and target scheme-version IDs equal the actual owning internal/external scheme versions of its concepts; it also states conditions, intended use, prohibited use, and information loss.
Claim-level cid governance is active when scope_namespace='cid', the predicate namespace is cid, or either endpoint resolves to a cid concept. Every such claim must use an active cid concept-scheme version; scope_scheme_type='none' is reserved for sealed non-semantic profiles.

title: Data Model
text:
Release and Approval Identity

releases.manifest_hash is immutable release-content identity and is finalized before V&V.
release_approval_packages are separate derivation artifacts created after current verification, validation, retrieval, and assurance exist. package_version plus supersedes_approval_package_id creates one ordered, immutable, non-forking chain per release, exposed by current_release_approval_packages. Each package’s snapshots exactly equal the deterministic release-relative closure of definitions, labels/forms/facets, semantic relations/predicates, mappings, sealed profiles/constraints/rules, approved uses, sealed query/relevance material, and current V&V/retrieval/assurance records.
approval_decisions and publication_events bind one exact current-head package ID; publication_events.attempted_manifest_hash carries that approval-package hash, not the release-content hash.

title: Data Model
text:
Derived State
current_claim_state, current_change_request_state, current_source_routing, current_verification_records, current_intended_uses, current_query_sets, current_retrieval_evaluations, current_validation_records, current_release_approval_packages, governed_item_state, current_published_releases, and published_claims are views over immutable events or supersession chains. Current state is never inferred from an older pass/fit, use/query/package version, claim row, or approval alone.

Migration Files

0001_initial.sql: canonical registries and constraints.
0002_invariants_and_views.sql: normalized views, indexes, and validation queries.
0003_transition_guards.sql: typed-ID, producer, domain, evidence-profile, role-separation, publication, retirement, and append-only triggers.

Their exact SHA-256 values are pinned in migrations/manifest.json.

title: CLI Specification
text:
Pipeline Commands
pipeline extract   --input SPEC.json
pipeline segment   --input SPEC.json
pipeline normalize --input SPEC.json
pipeline tokenize  --input SPEC.json
pipeline ngrams    --input SPEC.json
pipeline aggregate --input SPEC.json
pipeline observe   --input SPEC.json

Operation
Additional required contract




extract
source has source_version_id, adapter, and path; extraction has adapter profile, quality state/JSON, warnings, unreadable regions, and optional exact spans. Only plain, markdown, and external_import are accepted.


segment
selection identifies extracted text and source version. segmentation.mode is explicit, whole, line, or paragraph; explicit defaults/overrides supply origin, role, language, scope, actor/time/session fields. Every cid segment also supplies a domain-applicability and accepted-admission package.


normalize
selection names segment IDs or one source version; rules_path and optional rules_sha256 pin the normalization JSON. Non-English selection fails unless explicitly allowed.


tokenize
selection names normalized segment IDs/artifacts; rules pin token pattern and exact lemma map. Sentences and tokens share one output artifact.


ngrams
selection.token_artifact_version_ids; ngram_min, ngram_max, and form. Every n-gram stores each token and position.


aggregate
selection.occurrence_artifact_version_ids, occurrence_kind; explicit measures and optional provenance group_by. SF/IGF are unavailable when authenticated IDs are absent.


observe
occurrence selection, named window, observation predicate, optional explicit isolate nodes, and optional projections. Source-distribution scores create explicit similarity-signal records; projection endpoints are declared and root membership is copied exactly.


isf
evidence IDs or claim_id, independence_rule_id, analysis scope, optional reviewer. Unknown lineage is reported and excluded.



For the source-to-observation pipeline, run.inputs must name exactly the artifact versions selected by the operation; extra or omitted versions fail before any derivation record is written.
No pipeline count or score creates a candidate or semantic record.

title: Provenance and Assurance
text:
Acquisition obtains/authenticates source material. Derivation transforms registered artifact versions. They are different activities and never share an untyped execution string.
Every acquisition resolves:
activity -> procedure version
         -> tool version(s) or explicit no-tool rationale
         -> configuration version
         -> environment version
         -> actor + start/end
         -> source locator + authentication/completeness
         -> acquisition artifact -> source version
The selected configuration must be explicitly applicable to the activity’s procedure and each linked tool. Source routing is a separate reviewer/rationale/date/version decision history; the latest unsuperseded decision is current.
Every derivation resolves:
run -> input artifact membership/order/exact observed identity state+hash+rationale
    -> procedure version
    -> tool version membership/order or explicit no-tool rationale
    -> configuration version
    -> environment version
    -> actor + start/end + log/evidence
    -> output artifact membership/order/hash
    -> concrete rows with the same artifact/run IDs
The selected source artifacts for extraction, segmentation, normalization, tokenization, n-gram generation, aggregation, observation construction, release packaging, and approval-package finalization must exactly match the run-input artifact set. Each input explicitly repeats the artifact’s observed identity state, hash, and unavailable rationale; omission is invalid and no Python default silently fills the tuple. The database checks the full tuple plus procedure/tool configuration applicability and producer/run/output consistency. The Python validator independently recomputes those comparisons and retained local source bytes.

The selected source artifacts for extraction, segmentation, normalization, tokenization, n-gram generation, aggregation, observation construction, release packaging, and approval-package finalization must exactly match the run-input artifact set. Each input explicitly repeats the artifact’s observed identity state, hash, and unavailable rationale; omission is invalid and no Python default silently fills the tuple. The database checks the full tuple plus procedure/tool configuration applicability and producer/run/output consistency. The Python validator independently recomputes those comparisons and retained local source bytes.

title: Provenance and Assurance
text:
Source-to-Text Fidelity
Plain and Markdown adapters import UTF-8 text as-is. External extraction imports text produced elsewhere and requires the generic derivation envelope plus adapter profile, page/object-to-output span map, reading order, quality state, warnings, unreadable regions, and uncertainty. An extracted text binds its exact source version and source artifact input and retains a recomputable UTF-8 hash in artifact_content_identities, keyed by output artifact, producer run, content role, algorithm, and canonicalization. That byte-level content identity is deliberately distinct from the canonical extraction-bundle artifact identity. Every span repeats the chain and stays inside the text; every segment selects that text artifact as a derivation input, uses the same source/text and one covering span, and equals the exact half-open text slice. Corrected text and spans use new IDs and explicit correction links. The original is never overwritten.

title: Provenance and Assurance
Provenance and Assurance
text:
Evidence Classes







Class
Contract




E-SOURCE
Authenticated exact source/version or a segment from it.


E-DERIVED
Exact artifact, actual producing derivation, registered output, and compatible result hash.


E-DOMAIN
Typed normative/authoritative domain warrant and same authenticated source version are mandatory; informative warrants do not qualify.


E-PROJECT
Approved versioned CI-DIGITAL requirement is mandatory.


E-ANNOTATION
Interpretation only; never qualifying domain/project warrant.


E-REVIEW
Review/adjudication act; cannot create technical support circularly.


E-CHECK
Verification/validation result; pass/fail remains in the result record.


E-DECISION
Authorized governance action; approval does not prove the property.

title: Provenance and Assurance
text:
Recoverable Evidence Sets
aggregate_measure_evidence, observation_edge_evidence, and similarity_signal_evidence normalize exact evidence/source/segment membership. If an evidence item is named, its source and segment must be repeated exactly; if a segment is named, it must belong to the repeated source. evidence_set_hash is calculated from the canonical ordered membership; validators recompute both hash and anchor coherence. Every source-distribution edge has exactly one separate immutable similarity-signal record with the same endpoints, producer, and membership. A score formula may change only a new result/configuration, never membership or historical claim state.
Projection copies every membership row from its source edge and records observation_edge_derivations. It must preserve the hash and report independent_evidence_delta=0.

title: Provenance and Assurance
Provenance and Assurance
Provenance and Assurance
text:
Release Evidence Freeze
The release-content artifact is closed before V&V and never gains post hoc evidence. finalize-release instead creates a canonical derivation artifact whose immutable approval-package hash covers the content-manifest hash plus exact release-relative snapshots of definitions, labels/forms/facets, assertions/predicates, mappings, sealed profiles/constraints/rules, approved uses, sealed query/relevance records, current verification/validation/retrieval, and the assurance argument. Package versions form a linear explicit supersession chain for the unchanged release content; only the current head is eligible for a new approval or publication. Validators recompute every snapshot and both artifact hashes.

title: Deployment
text:
Prerequisites

CPython >=3.11 with standard-library sqlite3 linked to SQLite >=3.35.0.
A local account with read access to configured source roots and write access to this app’s var/ and exports/ directories.
No package installation and no network access.

An operator should verify these prerequisites independently before first use. runtime.lock.json is the pinned declared baseline; an environment_versions record captures the observed environment used for each run.

title: Deployment
text:
Local Startup
cd /home/fern/workspace/Inatel/CI-DIGITAL/worktree/software/ci-digital-concept-index
bin/ci-digital-concept-index status
bin/ci-digital-concept-index init
bin/ci-digital-concept-index record import \
  --input fixtures/bootstrap-registry.json
bin/ci-digital-concept-index validate integrity
status is read-only and reports pending migrations when the database does not exist. init refuses an existing database. The bootstrap adds governance/runtime registries only; it is not corpus data.

title: Deployment
Deployment
text:
State and Permissions

Recommended mode: app sources read-only after review; var/ and exports/ owner-write only.
SQLite DB, journal, WAL, Python caches, and generated exports are ignored by .gitignore.
Back up the database only while no writer is active, or use an independently reviewed SQLite backup procedure. Register backup/restoration acts when used as evidence.
Never place the database on an untrusted shared filesystem or expose the launcher through a network service.

title: Deployment
text:
Upgrade

Preserve the current app source, migration manifest, database, and successful release exports.
Review new migration SQL and manifest checksums.
Open a change request and impact assessment for schema/code/config changes.
Execute migrate only against a backup-qualified copy first.
Create the immutable release-content candidate, then re-verify deterministic behavior and re-validate current approved intended uses against current sealed query/relevance baselines.
Finalize the separate post-V&V approval-package version, explicitly superseding the current package when one exists, then approve and publish that exact current-head hash; never rewrite release content or package snapshots.

title: Deployment
text:
Rollback
Application rollback restores a reviewed prior source/runtime deployment without editing the evidence ledger. A channel’s first successful release is an explicit bootstrap event with bootstrap evidence and no rollback fields. Later successful replacement is advance from the immediate effective release. Release rollback is a separate publication_events row proving the rolled-back release was immediately current and naming a distinct prior successfully published target whose publication-bound package remains that release’s valid current head, plus the outgoing exact approval package, rollback procedure/version, evidence, actor, and time. A failed publication alone leaves current release unchanged.

title: Deployment
text:
Operational Verification
Follow ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md. Do not infer production readiness from successful initialization or a structurally valid database; semantic correctness and intended-use fitness require independent review and V&V records.

Source-to-Claim Chain
source_registry
 -> source_versions -> artifact_versions -> acquisition_activities
 -> extraction_runs/extracted_texts/spans -> derivation_runs
 -> segments -> evidence_items -> evidence_lineage_groups
 -> occurrences/measures/observation_edges + normalized memberships
 -> candidate + candidate observation links
 -> candidate_claim_links -> claims -> claim_evidence_links
 -> independence assessment/classes/claim link
 -> reviews -> claim_state_events
 -> semantic_assertions or mapping_registry
Every step retains exact IDs. The graph view is not the semantic claim view; it is reconstructed from immutable observation records.

title: Traceability
text:
Claim-to-Publication Chain
claim + exact sealed positive profile + typed evidence + current approved intended use + accepted review
 -> release_items(canonical record hashes) -> releases(non-recursive content artifact hash)
 -> verification_records
 -> validation_records(current use/user/context + sealed query/relevance FK)
 -> retrieval_evaluations(current sealed query/relevance FK)
 -> assurance_arguments and subclaims
 -> current-head release_approval_packages version + exact required release_baseline_snapshots
 -> approval_decisions(package ID) + approval_inputs
 -> publication_events(package hash + bootstrap/advance/rollback mode)
 -> current_published_releases / published_claims
Approval and successful publication are independently queryable. A failed event never appears in current_published_releases.

title: Traceability
text:
Change Impact Chain
change_request_items
 -> computed and declared dependency closure
 -> impact_items + closure hash
 -> stale claim events and reverify/revalidate obligation
 -> new V&V/review/release records
 -> deprecation or retirement decision
 -> tombstone
Historical source, evidence, claims, releases, and publication events remain resolvable throughout.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Static Delivery Checks








ID
Check
Pass condition




ST-01
Python source parse
Every .py parses through ast.parse; no module import or bytecode execution is required.


ST-02
Structured files parse
Every JSON file parses, and pyproject.toml parses.


ST-03
Migration inventory
Migration versions are unique/ordered; object names are unique; manifest hashes equal files.


ST-04
CLI/doc alignment
Every advertised command exists in cli.py; all four mandatory views exist in SQL/export allowlist; invalid arguments route to canonical JSON stderr and exit 3.


ST-05
Table/code alignment
Every table literal used by Python exists in migrations; every typed ID policy uses a constrained entity type.


ST-06
Runtime-state absence
No .sqlite, .sqlite3, journal, WAL, generated export, or Python cache exists in the delivered tree.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Acquisition and Provenance







ID
Required result




AP-01
100% of admitted segments traverse exact source artifact/input -> extraction run/output -> typed UTF-8 content identity and recomputed extracted-text hash -> segmentation input -> covering span -> identical half-open text slice and source version.


AP-02
100% of locally retained payload hashes recompute; unavailable artifact hashes carry explicit state and rationale.


AP-03
User, assistant, quotation, file, code, tool, system, and external classes remain query-separable.


AP-04
An assistant-only phrase has user TF/UF zero.


AP-05
Quoted VLSI text contributes to quotation/source views, never user-authored recurrence.


AP-06
Two records on one date with null sessions give date count one and SF unavailable.


AP-07
Mirror/quotation/summary/measure lineage remains traceable; every assessment member has one coherent class; claim-relative ISF collapses to one.


AP-08
Every cid segment/concept/claim resolves exact live target type, normalized typed facets, matching available basis-conditioned support, applicability, and accepted admission.


AP-09
Every source/derived artifact traverses the complete normalized acquisition/derivation spine, including source-routing history and matching acquisition status.


AP-10
Every dangling or inapplicable procedure/tool/config/environment/input/output/acquisition/run reference is rejected or release-blocking.


AP-11
Every derivation input explicitly records the exact observed identity state/hash/unavailable-rationale tuple; omission or disagreement with the artifact row is rejected.


AP-12
Text byte identity remains separate from extraction-bundle identity, and each aggregate/edge/similarity membership’s evidence/source/segment values resolve one exact provenance chain.


AP-13
Every release-item canonical record/hash recomputes; the non-recursive release-content hash equals manifest, artifact identity, and derivation output.


AP-14
Every approval-package version contains exactly the deterministic release-relative closure of definitions, labels/forms/facets, relations/predicates, mappings, sealed profiles/rules, approved uses, sealed query/relevance data, current V&V/retrieval, and assurance; later versions explicitly extend one current-head chain for the same release.


AP-15
A claim cannot bind an unsealed, changed, vacuous, zero-minimum, or wrong-version profile.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Deterministic Transformation







ID
Required result




DT-01
Two clean runs with byte-identical inputs, configuration, IDs, and timestamps produce equal rows and hashes.


DT-02
Every normalized character and token span maps to raw source text; raw text is unchanged.


DT-03
A score-only change cannot alter evidence membership, ISF, claim events, approval, or publication.


DT-04
Reconstructed observation_graph has exactly all registered nodes, including the isolate, and independent records for every source-distribution similarity signal.


DT-05
Projection lists source edge, identical root membership/hash, and independent delta zero.


DT-06
Sparse 2–4-gram input reports sparse output and creates no candidate automatically.


DT-07
DF counts source versions; ISF separately recomputes same-claim available supporting role/class families and collapses mirrors/revisions/derivatives under the profile’s named rule.


DT-08
External PDF/OCR import retains exact input/output hashes, procedures/tools/config/environment, spans, quality, warnings, and uncertainty.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Domain and Semantic Negative Tests







ID
Required result




DS-01
Generic software and IC/UVM “verification” remain distinct definitions/schemes.


DS-02
Construction/BIM digital twin is excluded from cid or retained only in an explicit ext scheme.


DS-03
Coverage/closure co-occurrence remains an observation; it creates no semantic predicate.


DS-04
Facet/scheme membership creates no hierarchy automatically.


DS-05
Identical external labels with different definitions cannot produce exact mapping.


DS-06
Model/rule relation suggestions remain candidates until an admissible separately reviewed claim exists.


DS-07
An accepted isolated VLSI concept remains in the published node inventory.


DS-08
Database/OAuth/build text in a VLSI container is not admitted by container location.


DS-09
Telecommunications text with shared labels remains outside cid absent exact VLSI applicability.


DS-10
Brazil/geography/policy text remains metadata, explicit ext, or excluded.


DS-11
A projected edge alone cannot enter reviewed_semantic_graph or satisfy a semantic release claim.


DS-12
Annotation/review/decision evidence or an informative warrant relabeled as qualifying E-DOMAIN/E-PROJECT is rejected; informative E-DOMAIN contributes to no count, ISF, reviewed graph, or release gate.


DS-13
Explicit cid scope, a cid predicate, or either cid endpoint activates one identical claim firewall; cid activation forces exact active cid scope, while scope none requires a sealed non-semantic profile.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Structural and Logical Checks







ID
Required result




SL-01
All release IDs are unique, typed, immutable, live, and resolvable; every tombstoned stable ID remains reserved.


SL-02
JSON fields parse; SQL foreign keys, checks, unique indexes, typed-ID triggers, transition guards, and append-only guards reject malformed writes.


SL-03
Claim type/version equals the exact recomputed seal of a profile with at least one positive requirement; every group and ISF floor recomputes from exact qualifying same-claim evidence; every independence link names that claim/evidence and matching rule.


SL-04
Every n-gram has exactly n ordered token memberships from position zero through n-1.


SL-05
Every aggregate, observation edge, and similarity signal exposes coherent exact evidence/source/segment membership and its membership hash recomputes.


SL-06
Every semantic edge uses a registered non-obs predicate and its exact accepted admissible claim.


SL-07
Every mapping references the actual owning source/target concept scheme versions, crosses distinct versions, and retains intended/prohibited use, conditions, comparison rationale, and loss.


SL-08
Observation, candidate, claim, semantic, retrieval, V&V, approval, publication, and lifecycle records remain separate and are joined only by typed links.


SL-09
Every release item resolves its declared family/version and exact canonical record/hash; the immutable content manifest equals its packaging artifact identity/output; every item remains live and every live graph node is included before approval.


SL-10
Publication binds the exact approved current-head package hash and current gates/inputs/role separation. First success is a no-rollback bootstrap with evidence; later success advances from the immediate effective same-channel release; rollback proves immediate current and prior-success target history and restores only a target whose previously published package remains its valid current head.


SL-11
View and release exports are stably ordered canonical JSON/TSV with SHA-256 sidecars; release export accepts only a currently published release whose exact publication-bound package remains the current valid head, and emits both identities plus frozen snapshots.


SL-12
Each source-to-observation derivation declares exactly the artifact versions selected by the operation; missing or extra run inputs are rejected before records are written.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Retrieval and Intended Use







ID
Required result




RU-01
The versioned query set covers supporting sources for SystemVerilog/UVM concepts, coverage distinctions, lifecycle artifact roles, DFT/test access, relation evidence/counterevidence, deprecated historical terms, and concept evolution without assistant-to-user leakage.


RU-02
Two VLSI/EDA reviewers independently judge a stratified sample; disagreement/adjudication, per-query precision/recall, macro/micro summaries, unanswerable queries, provenance errors, semantic false positives, and reviewer disagreement are retained.


RU-03
Semantic performance thresholds are set only after a baseline run, while the fixed release gate remains zero known provenance-class or domain-boundary violations.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Lifecycle and Release







ID
Required result




LC-01
Unresolved changed dependencies make affected claims stale and block a new release/use; history remains unchanged.


LC-02
A changed intended use/query set or later not-fit result requires a new current validation head; prior validation remains historical and cannot satisfy a gate.


LC-03
Superseded/withdrawn standards open change/impact work; claims never silently rebind.


LC-04
Live claims/mappings/published dependencies block retirement.


LC-05
Tombstoned IDs cannot be assigned to a new term, concept, claim, evidence item, or release.


LC-06
Failed publication has no state-changing fields and does not change current release; advance names the immediate effective prior release; rollback proves the rolled-back release was current and restores only a prior same-channel success whose published package remains its valid current head; effective events use strict (event_time, publication_event_id) order.


LC-07
Superseding an intended use, query set, relevance baseline, validation, or retrieval evaluation immediately makes older fitness evidence non-current; release requires matching user group/context and current sealed bindings.


LC-08
The first effective same-channel success is possible only as bootstrap with evidence and no rollback fields; bootstrap is impossible after effective history, and every later success is advance from the immediate current release.


LC-09
Release content remains immutable after V&V; separate immutable approval-package versions freeze current evidence in one explicit non-forking supersession chain, and approval/publication bind only the current head’s hash rather than mutating or substituting the content manifest.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Non-Functional Controls







ID
Required result




NF-01
In a clean supported Python environment, installation and every local command require only Python standard-library modules and SQLite and make no network request.


NF-02
Byte-identical clean inputs, configuration, explicit IDs, and timestamps produce byte-identical canonical rows, exports, and hashes.


NF-03
Malformed direct and workflow writes are rejected by the applicable foreign key, check, unique index, typed-ID trigger, transition gate, or append-only guard without altering prior rows.


NF-04
Missing, unavailable, partial, uncertain, and inconclusive values remain distinct from zero, pass, fit, approved, accepted, or published in records and exported views.


NF-05
Source and export path traversal outside configured roots is rejected, and database/generated operational state remains under configured app-local roots.


NF-06
Adversarial ingested text containing shell, SQL, Python, template, or configuration syntax remains inert data and is never dispatched for execution.


NF-07
User, assistant, quotation, file, code, tool, system, and external origin classes remain separately filterable in measures, evidence, views, and exports.


NF-08
Supersession, failed publication, rollback, deprecation, and retirement preserve all prior versions and successful historical releases as resolvable immutable records.

title: Acceptance Criteria
text:
Suggested Operator Protocol
After independent review of the fixture content, an operator may initialize a disposable database, load the bootstrap, instantiate each fixture case, execute narrowly scoped validators first, then validate all, compare canonical exports across clean runs, and retain logs/hashes as E-CHECK. That future execution—not this source delivery—establishes pass/fail evidence.
